poc.meshStats: Source hm08 base.obj: 19158 verts, 18486 quads. Kept: group 'body' (verts 0..13379, 13378 quads → 26756 tris) + helper-l-eye/helper-r-eye (72 verts / 70 quads each → 280 tris), giving 13524 kept (welded) vertices and 14677 render vertices after splitting UV seams. LOD0 has 27036 triangles. Dropped: helper-tights, skirt, hair, genital, the 4 eyelash helpers, and joint cubes. Teeth and tongue are optional ('keepMouth': true). Quads are split along the shorter base-mesh diagonal. LODs come from meshoptimizer 0.22 simplifyWithAttributes (normals as attributes), body-only, and are extra index buffers over the same render vertices. Triangle counts: LOD1 ratio 0.5 with face locked = 13658 (error 1.5 mm); LOD2 ratio 0.25 with face locked = 6968; LOD3 ratio 0.12 unlocked = 3490 (error 4 mm). Bones: 53 (game_engine). Skin: 0 unweighted vertices; 608 vertices had more than 4 influences and were truncated and renormalised. Shells per kit, in triangles after decimation with locked borders: jersey 1518, shorts 1000, socks 356, shoes 892, headband 312, hair 600, sleeve_r 797, eyebrows 120, beard 1176. Bytes: shared bin 627,668 B (402 KB gzip). That splits into topology+UV+skin+keptToObj 385,520 B, three LOD index buffers about 145 KB, and all shells about 98 KB. Per player: 108,192 B (Uint16x3 positions 81,144 + oct8 normals 27,048), which does not gzip. Header JSON is about 15 KB per player (bones, landmarks, macro list). Total for 6 players ≈ 627,668 + 6×108,192 = 1,276,820 B ≈ 1.22 MiB, plus about 75 KB of JSON, so under the 2 MB target. Quantisation step is 0.02–0.035 mm.
poc.macroSystem:
Implemented in lib/targets.mjs, driven by MPFB's CC0 targets/macrodetails/macro.json.

Splitting a slider value: for each 'part' of a slider where lowest < v < highest, t = (v-lowest)/(highest-lowest); the low name gets 1-t and the high name gets t (an empty name means no target). The parts are:
- gender: female..male over (-0.01, 1.01)
- age: baby..child (-0.01, 0.1874998), child..young (0.1874999, 0.49998), young..old (0.49999, 1.01). ageYears is converted as 1 y → 0, 11 y → 0.1875, 25 y → 0.5, 90 y → 1, linear in between.
- muscle: minmuscle..averagemuscle (<0.49998), averagemuscle..maxmuscle (>=0.49999)
- weight: minweight..averageweight / averageweight..maxweight (same breakpoints)
- height: minheight..'' over (-0.01, 0.49), then a dead zone, then ''..maxheight over (0.51, 1.01)
- proportions: uncommonproportions..'' over (-0.01, 0.4999), ''..idealproportions over (0.5, 1.01)

Race weights {african, asian, caucasian} are normalised to sum to 1.

Target files under targets/macrodetails/, kept only when the product weight is > 0.01 (the MPFB cutoff):
1. `<race>-<gender>-<age>` with weight w_race·w_g·w_a, e.g. african-male-young
2. `universal-<g>-<a>-<muscle>-<weight>` with weight w_g·w_a·w_m·w_w, e.g. universal-male-young-maxmuscle-averageweight
3. `height/<g>-<a>-<m>-<w>-<minheight|maxheight>` with weight w_g·w_a·w_m·w_w·w_h
4. `proportions/<g>-<a>-<m>-<w>-<uncommonproportions|idealproportions>` with the same product times w_p; 'baby' is skipped
Female-only breast targets are not used. For a fully male, young body you need 3 race files, 9 universal files, 18 height files and 18 proportions files.

Order of application: macro targets, then detail targets (pos += w·delta in OBJ decimetres, Y up), then ×0.1 to metres, then a uniform scale = height/rawHeight. Finally the soles are moved to y=0 and the pelvis z to 0.

macro.height can be 'auto': an 18-step bisection picks the slider value whose raw MakeHuman height equals the requested height, so the final scale stays at 1.0. Results: test A got slider 0.9644, test B got 0.5732.

Validation: rebuilding the default MakeHuman (all sliders 0.5, races 1/3 → 8 targets) reproduces every rig default_position to 0.00 mm (Root excluded). This confirms axes (blender = (x, -z_obj, y_obj)·0.1), units and the weighting maths.

Baked heights, measured as max y of the CPU-skinned mesh: tall = 2.290 m, athlete = 1.880 m.

poc.rigNotes:
Rig: game_engine (rig.game_engine.json), 53 bones, stored parents-first.
- Root(-1) > pelvis
- pelvis > thigh_l > calf_l > foot_l > ball_l, and the same chain for _r
- pelvis > spine_01 > spine_02 > spine_03
- spine_03 > neck_01 > head
- spine_03 > clavicle_l|r > upperarm_l|r > lowerarm_l|r > hand_l|r
- each hand_l|r > thumb_01 > 02 > 03, index_01..03, middle_01..03, ring_01..03, pinky_01..03

There are no jaw or eye bones; eyes and teeth are weighted to head.

Joint positions are evaluated per player on the morphed 19158-vertex mesh, so joint cubes follow all targets. Strategies:
- CUBE: mean of the 8 vertices of vertex group cube_name from basemesh_vertex_groups.json (inclusive [start, end] ranges)
- MEAN: mean of vertex_indices
- VERTEX: vertex_index
- anything else: default_position mapped as obj = (x, z, -y)/0.1

In this rig every bone head and tail is CUBE except Root.tail, which is MEAN. Root.head is forced to the origin (0,0,0).

Per player the header stores bones[i] = {head, tail, roll} in metres. tail is the child joint; roll is Blender's roll, kept only so Blender-style frames can be rebuilt.

Runtime rest pose is MakeHuman's A-pose (arms about 45° down) with identity rest rotations: bone.position = head - parentHead. Local axes are therefore the character axes (+x = character's left, +y up, +z forward). Verified poses:
- upperarm_l.rotation.z = +2.35 and upperarm_r.rotation.z = -2.35 put the arms overhead (with clavicle ±0.25)
- calf_r.rotation.x = +π/2 bends the knee 90°; thigh_r.rotation.x = -0.8 lifts the thigh forward
- spine_01/02/03.rotation.y = 0.17/0.17/0.18 gives a 30° twist; neck_01.y and head.y = 0.3 turn the head
- fingers curl with rotation.x
p.boneAxis(name) returns tail-head for twist rotations.

Skin weights come from weights.game_engine.json ({weights: {bone: [[vertex, w]...]}}, CC0): top 4 per vertex, renormalised, quantised to Uint8 with each vertex summing to exactly 255. Body and shells are SkinnedMeshes bound to one Skeleton per player, which means one bone texture.

Deformation of the posed bodies, both bare and clothed, shows no tearing. Linear blend skinning flattens the deltoid a little with arms overhead. Landmarks exported per player (joint-cube means): l-eye, r-eye, mouth, jaw, head, head-2, neck, l/r-hand-2, l/r-hand-3, l/r-scapula, l/r-foot-2, pelvis. These are useful for the ball anchor, gaze and camera framing.
poc.runtimeFormat:
Full spec is in tools/legends/FORMAT.md. The bake writes <name>.json (header), <name>.shared.bin and <name>.<id>.bin per player. All data is little-endian with 4-byte-aligned sections described as {offset, count, type, itemSize, bytes}.

Shared bin sections:
- renderToKept: u16 per render vertex
- uv: u16n×2. MakeHuman atlas UV for the body. The eyes are re-projected to a front disc: (0.5, 0.5) is the pupil and radius 0.5 is the eyeball.
- index: u16×3, LOD0, with groups [{name: body, material: skin, start, count}, {name: eyes, material: eye, …}]
- skinIndex: u8×4 per kept vertex
- skinWeight: u8n×4 per kept vertex
- keptToObj: u16, for future runtime morphs
- lod1..3.index: u16×3; header.lods[] = {ratio, lockHead, triangles, bodyTriangles, error, section, groups}
- shell.<name>.{a, b (u16), t (u8n), uv (u16n*2, range 0..2 for the wrapped seam), offsetScale (u8n*4), edge (u8n*0.1m), index (u16×3), cover (u16 kept vertices)}; header.shells[] = {name, kind, material, offset, relax, uvMode, vertexCount, triCount, sections}

Per player bin: position (u16q×3: posMin + q·posStep) and normal (oct8×2), both per kept vertex. header.players[] = {id, label, file, bytes, sections, height, scale, rawHeight, posMin, posStep, bones[{head, tail, roll}], landmarks, macro, macroTargets, targets, appearance}. header.bones = [{name, parent}]; header.counts = {renderVertices 14677, keptVertices 13524, bodyKeptVertices 13380, triangles 27036, bones 53}.

Loader API (tools/legends/loader-prototype.js, imports '../../vendor/three.module.js'):
- `const lib = await loadLegends(headerUrl)` returns {header, players: [ids], shellNames, createPlayer, getPlayerData}. The shared UV, index, skin and LOD-index attributes are reused across every player geometry.
- `const p = await lib.createPlayer(id, {lod, materials: {skin, eye, mouth}, shells: {jersey: mat, …}, shellOffsets: {name: +m}, shellFade: {hair: 0.008, beard: 0.01}, hideCovered: true})` returns {id, info, object: THREE.Group, mesh: SkinnedMesh (material array per group), skeleton, bones: {name: THREE.Bone}, shells: {name: SkinnedMesh}, setLod(n), resetPose(), boneAxis(name), landmark(name)}.

Behaviour:
- Each player's bin is fetched once and its geometry is cached, so two instances of the same player share it.
- frustumCulled is false on skinned meshes; cull the whole player yourself.
- Shells get position/normal/uv/skinIndex/skinWeight, plus 'edge' (normalised, 1.0 = 0.1 m) and, when shellFade is set, an RGBA 'color' whose alpha ramps up from the boundary. Use it with material.vertexColors and alphaTest.
- hideCovered removes body triangles whose 3 kept vertices are all in the worn shells' cover lists. The result is cached per player × LOD × shell set.
poc.clothingHairPlan:
All clothing and hair are shells built from the shared body topology in lib/shells.mjs.

Each shell region is a signed function f(v) (> 0 inside), evaluated once on the unmorphed base.obj. Inputs are skin-weight masks and base.obj landmarks in metres (eyeY .728, browY .752, noseTipY .694, mouthY .668, underChinY .616, headCZ .057, clavY .519, shoulder (±.168, .525), armpitY .40, pelvisY .073, kneeY -.369, ankleY -.745, ear box y .686–.742, z .026–.068, |x| > .071).

Body triangles are clipped at f = 0 (marching triangles). Shell vertices are therefore body vertices or points on body edges (a, b, t), so cut lines are smooth and not stair-stepped along quads. At runtime: position = lerp(P[a], P[b], t) + n·offset·offsetScale(v), using each player's own P/N, so one shared definition fits every body. Skin weights are the t-blend of a and b. UVs are a cylinder around the torso or a sphere around the head; seam triangles are duplicated with u+1. Optional meshopt decimation keeps the borders locked. A geodesic edge distance is stored for hairline fades and trims, and a 'cover' list of body vertices hidden under the shell.

Cloth relax (loader): Laplacian smoothing (jersey 12 iterations at 0.5, shorts 60 at 0.7) that may only push vertices outward from their minimum offset, so fabric bridges the buttock cleft, crotch and chest.

Shells built:
- jersey: tank top. Ellipse neck hole 1.2 cm deep at the back and 4.2 cm in front; ellipse armholes 3 cm below the armpit; hem at pelvis-0.15 overlapping the shorts. Offset 7 mm growing to ×2.8 toward the hem so it hangs. Cover inset 2.5 cm.
- shorts: waist at pelvis+0.085 down to 6.5 cm above the knee; offset 1 cm growing to ×3.8 at the hem.
- socks: ankle-1 cm to ankle+13 cm.
- shoes: placeholder.
- headband: ring 2.6–5.6 cm above the brow, tilted up toward the back.
- hair: scalp shell with a hairline function of azimuth (forehead +7 cm above the eyes, temples, sideburns in front of the ear, over the ear, nape) and the ear excluded.
- sleeve_r: compression sleeve from 13 cm below the shoulder to the wrist.
- eyebrows: arch strips above each eye.
- beard: under the nose to the cheekbones and sideburns, under the jaw, lips cut out.

Hair, beard and eyebrows use procedural canvas strand textures, shellFade vertex alpha and alphaTest 0.5. The jersey uses a canvas texture with the number on front and back and side stripes.

What the prototype showed (screenshots clothes_*.png):
- The tank top looks like a real jersey from front and back, and the shorts read as basketball shorts.
- Headband, beard and short hair work on both bodies from the same shared data.
- The posed frame (arms overhead, knee 90°, 30° twist) deforms with the body. Hiding covered body triangles removed hip-crease poke-through under the shorts and also cuts body triangles (LOD0 with a full kit is 25.6k triangles per player instead of 27k).

Limits:
- Shoes as a foot shell look like black feet with toes. Use a separate procedural or modelled sneaker mesh, rigid-skinned to foot_*/ball_*.
- Hair and beard are solid-looking caps or stubble. Fine for buzz cuts (Kobe, Jordan bald, LeBron, Kyrie, Yao short), but for volume (Giannis curls, high tops) add a second, larger-offset shell with alpha cards or a noise-displaced offsetScale.
- Paint stubble, hairline shadow and brows into a per-player skin texture to soften shell edges.
- A small jersey/shorts junction slit is still visible in extreme twists.
poc.perf:
Test setup: headless Chromium with SwiftShader, 844×390 at DPR 1. Six instances are re-posed every frame on a court plane under a broadcast camera; each frame ends with readPixels to force GPU completion. Times are averages over 20 frames. SwiftShader runs the vertex shader (skinning) on the CPU, so absolute numbers are 10–50× slower than a phone GPU; compare them relative to each other.

| scene | draw calls | triangles | ms/frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty scene | 1 | 2 | 14.6 |
| current-style primitive stand-ins (6 × 11 primitives) | 67 | 6.4k | 20–25 |
| legends LOD0, bodies only | 13 | 162k | 172 |
| legends LOD0, full kit (9 shells, covered body triangles hidden) | 67 | 154k | 174 |
| LOD1 + kit | 67 | 102k | 123–131 |
| LOD2 + kit | 67 | 81k | 105 |
| LOD3 + kit | 67 | 54k | 90 |

Cost scales roughly with triangles and vertices. CPU cost of posing 6 skeletons (rotations + updateMatrixWorld + skeleton.update): 0.5–0.85 ms per frame.

Draw calls are 2 body groups (skin, eyes) plus 1 per worn shell per player. Merging jersey, shorts, socks and shoes into one atlas material would cut this to about 4 per player.

LOD quality (lod.png):
- LOD1 (0.5, face locked, 13.7k triangles) is visually identical at full-body framing.
- LOD2 (0.25, face locked, 7k) keeps the face but the torso shows faceted shading (pecs).
- LOD3 (0.12, unlocked, 3.5k) is fine at broadcast distance, but the face loses likeness up close.
- Locking the whole head instead of just the face makes low LODs collapse the body (8.4k triangles, ugly), so use face-only locking.

Recommendation: LOD1 + kit (about 17k triangles per player, 102k total) for gameplay; LOD0 for replays and close-ups; LOD2 for far or low-end devices. A dynamic setLod is supported (index swap only, no per-player data).
risks: Likeness to the six real players is not solved by this pipeline. It provides the knobs: about 250 detail modifiers, macros, skin colour, hair and beard shells. The next phase needs careful per-player tuning against reference photos. Avoid real logos and team marks; use fictional or generic uniforms.
Shoes as a body-offset shell look like black feet with toes. A separate procedural or modelled sneaker mesh rigidly skinned to foot_*/ball_* is needed.

Hair is a thin scalp shell. It is good for buzz cuts and bald heads (Jordan, Kobe, LeBron, Yao, Kyrie short) but weak for Giannis-style curls or volume. Needs a second, larger-offset shell with alpha strands or displaced offsetScale. Shell edges can still look hard; paint stubble and hairline into a per-player skin texture too.

Region functions in lib/shells.mjs are hand-tuned to hm08 base.obj landmarks. They are shared across players, so extreme morphs such as huge head-scale could misplace hairline or ear cut-outs slightly.
Linear blend skinning: some deltoid flattening with arms overhead, and a candy-wrapper risk if forearm or neck twists exceed about 60°. Spread twist over chains, as done for the spine.

Cloth shells follow the body's skinning. Extreme poses (deep squat, thigh above 90°) can still make shorts hug the thigh or open small slits at the jersey/shorts junction; hideCovered removes skin poke-through, not cloth/cloth interpenetration.

SwiftShader numbers are relative only. 100–150k skinned triangles plus about 67 draw calls should be fine on recent phones but must be checked on a low-end Android device. Keep LOD switching and allow shadows only on a cheap proxy.
Per-player bins (108 KB) do not gzip. Six players total about 1.28 MB raw (shared bin 402 KB gzipped). Delta-encoding positions against base.obj would compress well if size becomes an issue.
SkinnedMesh.frustumCulled is disabled (bounds change with poses). Cull per player with your own bounding sphere.

test/scratch/ is gitignored by the game's .gitignore, so the PoC page, shoot.cjs, textures.js and baked assets there are not committed. The implementation phase must place baked assets under a shipped path (e.g. assets/legends/) and port the procedural textures into src.
meshoptimizer (MIT, npm 0.22.0) is an optional offline dependency installed into tools/legends/node_modules (gitignored). Without it the bake produces no LODs and no shell decimation.
The MPFB master branch can change upstream. Pin to a commit SHA in fetch.mjs BASE_URL if reproducibility matters (fetching currently uses master).

profiles.era: 2008-2010 #24 era (back-to-back title years, 2009 and 2010 Finals; age 30-31). This is the most recognisable look for three reasons. (1) It is the iconic 'Mamba' version: a shaved head, the jaw-jut scowl that became famous in the 2009 Finals and was modelled for the NBA 2K10 cover, and finger tape on the right hand. (2) The #24 gold/purple look dominates current memorabilia and memorial imagery. (3) It fixes the silhouette as a lean, long-limbed adult who is more filled out than the skinny #8 'afro' years (1996-2000) and the #8 headband years (2000-06). The #8 look (headband, slightly fuller face) is a good alternate skin, but the late-#24 look reads as 'Kobe' most reliably at a distance and in close-ups. Within the era, the default is no headband: he dropped it after the #8 years.

profiles.build: Lean, wiry-athletic swingman with a long-limbed 'whip' build. He is noticeably narrower and less massive than LeBron or Giannis, and more filled out than his #8 rookie self. Shoulders are moderately broad but sloped (not boxy), with well-rounded, defined deltoids and a visible trapezius line rising into a LONG, slender neck with prominent sternocleidomastoid cords. The chest is flat-to-moderately muscled (pectorals defined, not thick) and the torso is fairly shallow front-to-back. The waist is narrow, so the V-taper is clear, and the abdomen is flat with very low body fat. Arms are long (wingspan about 13 cm over height): biceps are lean, forearms ropey, and wrists slim. Hands are large with long fingers. Legs are long relative to the torso: lean, defined quads, slim knees, and narrow, relatively thin calves with slim ankles (a 'high-calf' look). Feet are large (about US 14). Compared with a generic 1.98 m athlete: about 8% narrower through the waist and hips, a longer neck, longer forearms and shins, less bulk in chest and thighs, and very low facial and body fat (hollow cheeks). Default posture: a slight forward head carry with chin often pushed forward, and loose, slightly rounded shoulders when walking.
profiles.face: HEAD SHAPE: long, narrow oval. Face height is clearly greater than width, and the crown is smooth and rounded with a gently rounded occiput, all very visible because the head is shaved. The face tapers slightly from cheekbones to a strong, long lower face. FOREHEAD: high and fairly smooth, gently sloped back, with mild temple recession at the hairline corners. BROW: moderate supra-orbital ridge. Eyebrows are dark, medium-thick and fairly straight with only a slight arch, set low and close over the eyes, so the face reads stern even at rest. They pull down and inward in the scowl. EYES: almond-shaped, medium-small and slightly deep-set under the brow, with mildly hooded upper lids and medium spacing. Iris dark brown (#2B1A12), sclera slightly warm. Outer corners are level to slightly up. Mild under-eye fullness at age 30. The look is an intense, narrow-eyed stare. NOSE: medium-long with a straight, medium-low bridge (no hump). The lower third widens to a rounded, moderately bulbous tip with flared alae. Nostrils are medium-wide and roughly horizontal in profile. Nose width at the alae is about equal to the inner-canthus distance plus 25%. LIPS/MOUTH: wide mouth. Lips are medium-full; the lower lip is fuller and slightly everted, and the upper lip is defined with a soft cupid's bow. Mild forward protrusion of the mouth region. Corners are neutral to slightly down at rest. Nasolabial folds are visible because the cheeks are lean. JAW/CHIN: THE key feature. A strong, long mandible with well-defined angles and a prominent, rounded-square chin that projects forward. Even at rest the chin sits slightly forward. In the signature 'jaw jut' the whole lower jaw thrusts forward and up by about 1-1.5 cm, the lower lip pushes over the upper or the bottom teeth are bared, and the chin lifts. CHEEKBONES: high and prominent, with hollows beneath them (low buccal fat), giving an angular, chiselled midface. EARS: medium-sized and slightly protruding (noticeable on the shaved head), with rounded helix and medium lobes, set at normal height. Faint 'skull' definition at the temples. TYPICAL ON-COURT EXPRESSION: the 'Mamba' face, meaning a set, unsmiling mouth, lowered brows, chin forward and eyes locked on the target. After big shots: the jaw jut with bared lower teeth and a slow nod. Rarely smiles mid-game; any smile is a wide, toothy grin.

signatureMoves: TURNAROUND FADEAWAY from the right block or mid-post, back to the basket, over the LEFT shoulder toward the baseline (30 fps, about 1.4 s). F0 catch: feet about 0.75 m apart, knees flexed 45 deg, pelvis lowered 0.10 m, spine01-03 flexed forward 20 deg in total, ball at the right hip (right hand on top/behind, left hand on the side), head yawed 35 deg left looking over the left shoulder at the rim. F0-6 fake: dip the right shoulder (spine02 roll -12 deg, spine03 yaw -20 deg toward the middle); the ball sweeps to the left hip, the head follows, and weight shifts 70% onto the right foot (pelvis translates 0.08 m right). F6-9 hold: the defender bites. F9-15 spin: LEFT foot is the pivot (the forefoot stays planted and rotates). Pelvis yaws +160 deg toward the baseline (over the left shoulder); the right thigh abducts/extends and swings the right foot around in an arc to land 0.6 m away, so the feet end shoulder-width, square to the rim and about 15 deg open to the baseline. Spine counter-rotates 20 deg late (the torso finishes after the pelvis). Ball travels from the hip to the chest with both hands and the elbows tucked. F15-19 load: knees flex to 65 deg, hips back, spine01 upright, ball rises to the chin, eyes locked on the rim. F19-25 takeoff from both feet: thighs and calves extend explosively, pelvis rises 0.50 m by the apex and translates 0.45 m AWAY from the rim and 0.10 m toward the baseline. Pelvis pitches back 15-20 deg and spine01 extends, so the upper body leans back. The legs swing forward with knees bent 25-35 deg, feet together or slightly split, and toes pointing at the rim (the body is a slight 'C' facing the basket). The right upperarm raises to 165 deg flexion, the right elbow goes 95 deg to 60 deg at the set point above the right forehead (ball about 15 cm above and 10 cm in front of the forehead), the left hand stays on the side of the ball, and the head stays level. F25-27 release near the apex: the right lowerarm extends to straight, the right hand wrist flexes 70 deg (snap) and the fingers curl down. The left guide hand peels off laterally 10 cm with the thumb up and fingers spread. The ball leaves at about 3.0 m with a 47-50 deg launch and backspin. F27-42: hold the follow-through ('hand in the cookie jar') while drifting back; the legs reach down. F42 landing: both feet hit about 0.5 m behind takeoff, knees absorb to 40 deg, arms lower over 6 frames, and a 0.1 m stumble-step back is allowed. Mirror variant: from the left block, spin over the right shoulder with the right foot as pivot.

JAB-SERIES INTO PULL-UP JUMPER (triple threat at the right wing or elbow, about 1.6 s). F0 triple threat: LEFT foot is the pivot, feet 0.6 m apart, knees 40 deg, ball at the right hip-pocket with the right hand on top, elbows out, spine02 forward 25 deg, chin forward. F0-5 jab 1: the right foot steps 0.35 m straight at the defender (right thigh flexes 30 deg and lands on the forefoot), the ball sways 0.2 m to the right, spine leans forward 10 deg and the head dips 5 cm. F5-10 recover: the right foot snaps back to the stance and the ball returns to the hip. F10-14 jab 2 (shorter, 0.2 m, quicker), with a sharp head fake upward (neck and head pitch up 10 deg, shoulders rise 3 cm). F14-16 rocker: the defender closes out. F16-20 rip-through: the ball sweeps low across the knees from the right hip to the left hip and back up through the chest, with both elbows high. F20-26 rise: a straight-up jumper from both feet (pelvis +0.55 m vertical, no fade), with the set point and release identical to the fadeaway but the torso vertical. F26-40 follow-through and land on the same spot. AI branch: after jab 2, if the defender sags, shoot. If the defender lunges, chain to 'jab-and-go': the right foot crosses past the defender's hip and the ball pushes out with the right hand before the left (pivot) foot lifts.

PUMP FAKE TO SIDE-STEP OR ONE-DRIBBLE PULL-UP (elbow or baseline, about 1.3 s). F0-6 pump: the ball rises from the chest to the shooting set point (right upperarm 0 to 140 deg) with the heels lifting 3 cm, but the knees stay flexed 30 deg and the pelvis rises only 0.04 m. Eyes go up to the rim and the shoulders shrug 3 cm. F6-9 the ball snaps back down to the chest. F9-14 one hard dribble with the right hand, pushed 0.9 m to the right (or left) and forward. The right foot leads the step; the left foot drags then plants as the 'hop'. Body lowers to knees 60 deg and the torso leans 20 deg into the direction of travel. F14-17 1-2 stop: the left foot plants then the right, with the plant foot 0.15 m ahead to stop momentum; pelvis decelerates and spine01 extends to upright. F17-30 jumper: vertical rise of 0.5 m and a slight forward drift of about 0.1 m, release at the apex. F30-40 follow-through and land.

BASELINE SPIN TO REVERSE LAYUP OR SPIN FADE (from the right baseline facing the rim, about 1.2 s). F0-4 drive: right-hand dribble toward the baseline, torso 25 deg forward, left shoulder leading. F4-8 plant: the LEFT foot plants hard at 45 deg (the pivot) and the ball is gathered into both hands at the right hip. F8-14 reverse spin: pelvis yaws -180 deg (spinning back over the right shoulder toward the middle) around the left foot; the right leg swings around and the ball is protected high and tight at the chest, elbows wide. F14-18 two-foot or right-foot-plant gather. Branch A (rim): a left-foot takeoff off the right plant, a reverse lay-up on the far side of the rim (right arm extends up and back, wrist flick with spin off the glass), head tilted back to see the rim. Branch B: a stop into the fadeaway from the frame-F19 sequence of Move 1.

ONE-HAND TOMAHAWK DUNK ON THE BREAK (right hand, about 1.0 s from the last dribble). F0 last dribble with the right hand at the free-throw line extended. F0-6 gather: two steps (right then left), with the ball cupped in the right hand against the right forearm. F6 takeoff off the LEFT foot (the right knee drives up to 100 deg hip flexion, the left leg extends fully, the left arm swings up for balance). F6-12 rise and cock: the right upperarm goes from 90 to 175 deg flexion and back behind the head, with the elbow bent 110 deg so the ball sits behind the right ear. The torso arches back 15 deg, the head tilts up and the jaw juts. Peak pelvis rise is 0.85 m (hand about 0.25 m above the rim). F12-15 slam: the right arm whips forward and down (shoulder flexion 175 to 120 deg, elbow extends), the wrist snaps and the ball goes through the rim. The hand grips the rim for 3 frames, then releases. F15-28 land on both feet, knees 50 deg. Post-dunk: Mannerism 1 (jaw jut and nod). Variant: a TWO-HAND REVERSE BASELINE DUNK. Run along the baseline, take off from both feet under the rim facing away from it, with the ball over the head in both hands. Spine extends back 25 deg and the head tilts back to see the rim. Both arms go from 180 deg flexion to extension behind the head, slamming backwards.

CROSSOVER HESITATION INTO STEP-BACK OR PULL-UP (top or wing, about 1.4 s). F0-4 hesitation: an upright 'walk' dribble with the right hand, torso rising 5 cm and a slight lean back that sells a stop. F4-8 burst: a low crossover from right to left (the ball bounces 0.3 m in front of the body, then hand-to-hand), dropping the pelvis 12 cm and the right foot pushing off. F8-12 a second dribble with the left hand, then a step-back: the left foot plants forward, then pushes the body back 0.7 m. Both feet land square, knees 55 deg, ball gathered at the chest. F12-24 a vertical jumper with a slight backward drift, standard release. A between-the-legs (right to left) variant: the ball passes between the feet while the right foot is forward.
profiles.shootingForm: Right-handed. Feet: shoulder-width, right foot slightly ahead (about 5 cm), toes turned about 10 deg left of the rim line. Dip: a short dip to waist height on catch-and-shoot; the ball rises along the body midline-to-right. Set point: just above and in front of the right forehead, ball about 12-15 cm above the eyebrows, the right elbow under the ball and aligned (tucked, slight 5-10 deg outward flare at most), and the upperarm about 10 deg above horizontal at the set point. Guide hand: the left hand on the side of the ball, thumb roughly vertical; it releases slightly before the shot and does not push. Release: at or just before the apex (a 'one-motion-plus' high release, not a set shot). Release hand height is about 3.0 m on a jumper and about 2.95 m on a fade (it does not drop much because he leans back). Follow-through: full elbow extension and a strong wrist snap with the fingers pointing down at the rim, held about 0.4-0.5 s, often still held while landing. Arc: medium-high, about 47-50 deg launch, apex about 4.4 m on a 5 m shot. Jump height: pelvis rise 0.45-0.55 m on standard jumpers (an athletic jump, not a 'no-jump' shooter). Fade: 0.3-0.6 m backward drift, with the torso leaning back 15-20 deg, legs swung slightly forward and knees bent, sometimes legs split (one knee higher). Quirks: the chin juts toward the rim at release; the eyes stay on the rim through the follow-through; on tough shots he releases with the body still rotating (spin fade). Free throw: right toe at the centre nail of the line with the right foot slightly forward. He takes three dribbles, gives the ball a short spin in his hands to find the seams, takes a deep breath (shoulders rise and fall 3 cm), bends his knees about 30 deg and shoots in one smooth motion with a small heel lift. He holds the follow-through until the ball reaches the rim.
mannerisms: JAW JUT (the 2009 Finals signature): after a big make, the lower jaw thrusts forward and up 1-1.5 cm (chin-prognathism target to +1.0, or the jaw bone forward), the lower lip pushes up over the upper lip or the lower teeth are bared, and the chin lifts 10 deg. Then a slow, deliberate nod 2-3 times while backpedalling on defence. Hold about 1.5 s.
The 'Mamba stare' at rest: unsmiling, brows lowered 2-3 mm and drawn in, eyes narrowed, chin slightly forward, head tilted down 5 deg. This is the default close-up face.
Biting or chewing the jersey collar: lifts the neckline of the jersey into his mouth with the right hand during dead balls or free throws by others; neck flexes forward 15 deg.
Hands on the hips of his shorts, or tugging the shorts' hem at the knees while bent over, during free throws or timeouts. Torso bent forward 40 deg and head up watching.
After a clutch shot: jogs back holding up the right index finger (or several fingers for a count) with an emotionless face, or gives a big fist-clench with the arm pumping down and the teeth bared.
'Kobe shrug/headshake': after an unstoppable fade, a small shrug and a dismissive headshake while backpedalling.
On defence before an inbound: crouches very low, wide, with the right hand slapping the floor once, or with arms wide and feet buzzing.
Wipes sweat from his face with the bottom of his jersey, or wipes his palms on his socks before free throws.
Free-throw routine as in shootingForm: three dribbles, ball spin, deep breath, then shoot and hold the follow-through.
Idle: a slight forward head carry, rolling his neck and shoulders, and flexing the taped right fingers (opening and closing his hand).
profiles.tendencies: An isolation scorer with a takeover mentality and high usage. On offence, the shot mix should be about 45% mid-range (elbows, wings, baseline and short corners), about 25% drives and finishes, about 15% post-ups, and about 15% threes (mostly pull-ups and late-clock). Preferred spots: right elbow, right wing, left/right block mid-post (turnaround fade over the shoulder toward the baseline) and the right baseline. Default sequence: catch, triple threat, jab series or pump fake, then a pull-up or fade. He keeps attacking regardless of the defender, with a high contested-shot tolerance (shoots over contests). The fadeaway probability rises with defender proximity and when the shot clock or game clock is under 6 s. In the clutch (last 2 minutes, close score) his usage spikes to near 100% and his pass probability drops. Drives right more (60/40), finishing with reverse lay-ups and spin moves, and dunks hard in transition (tomahawk). Passing: competent but shoot-first. He kicks out to an open teammate if double-teamed (60% of the time), otherwise splits or fades. On defence: an elite, aggressive on-ball defender who takes the opponent's best perimeter scorer. He uses a low, wide stance, denies hard on the wings, jumps passing lanes (high steal attempts with some gambles) and plays chase-down blocks from behind. Weak as help-side rim protection; avoids switching onto the biggest players. Rebounds only long ones and leaks out early in transition after a defensive stop.

likenessPriorities: Head silhouette: a smooth shaved/buzzed dark-stubble scalp on a long, narrow oval head, carried forward on a long slender neck with the chin pushed forward. This is the most readable cue at 120 px.

Kit and accessory signature: #24 gold (home) or purple (away) with contrasting numbers, a BLACK RIGHT-ARM SLEEVE, white-taped right index and middle fingers, no headband, and low-top shoes with mid-calf socks. At gameplay distance the sleeve plus #24 colours reads as 'Kobe' instantly.

Movement signature: the turnaround fadeaway (lean back 15-20 deg, legs forward, high release with a held follow-through), jab series and pump fakes, plus the jaw-jut-and-nod celebration. The animation sells the likeness as much as the mesh does.

Lower face: a strong, forward-projecting, long chin and well-angled mandible (chin-prominent and prognathism), high prominent cheekbones with hollow cheeks, and a set, unsmiling wide mouth with medium-full lips and a thin moustache plus small goatee. The jaw-jut expression is the key close-up feature.

Eyes, nose and skin, plus a lean long-limbed build: low straight brows over slightly deep-set, narrowed almond eyes; a straight medium bridge into a rounded, flared lower nose; warm medium-brown skin (#8B5A3C); and a wiry V-taper body with long arms (wingspan > height), a narrow waist and slim calves.

profiles.era: 1995-98, the second three-peat and the "Last Dance" season (ages 32-35). This is the look most people picture when they think of Jordan: a fully shaved, shiny bald head, a thin moustache with a small goatee, number 23 in red/black or white/red/black, long baggy shorts, black/white patent-leather shoes and one wristband. It also matches the most-replayed moments: the 1997 Flu Game, the 1998 Last Shot fadeaway over Russell, and the 72-10 season. His most famous dunk, the 1988 free-throw-line dunk, is reused as a stylised slam in the same 1990s look, because it is the Jumpman image fans know best. Optional alternates: 1991-93 (bald, thinner moustache, slimmer face, early "Shrug" era); 1984-88 rookie (short hair with receding hairline, number 23, shorter shorts), as an unlockable skin only.

profiles.build:
He is a lean, long-limbed wing who carries 98 kg without looking heavy. Differences from a generic 1.98 m athlete:
(1) Arms: unusually long for his height. Wingspan is about 2.11 m, an ape index of +13 cm, so his fingertips hang near mid-thigh to the top of the knee cap.
(2) Hands: very large, about 24.7 cm long. He palms the ball easily and cradles it in his forearm.
(3) Shoulders: broad but sloping. The deltoids are rounded and defined, not bodybuilder-capped. The 1990s Tim Grover strength programme added visible upper-chest and lat mass compared with his 1980s frame. The torso is a clear V: wide lats tapering to a very narrow waist (about 81 cm), with no belly.
(4) Torso: relatively short. The legs are long, especially the thighs, so the hip line sits high and the shorts' hem falls only just above the knee.
(5) Legs: lean, powerful thighs (quads defined, not bulky) and slender, long-tendon calves with thin ankles. The knees look bony.
(6) Neck: long and medium-thick, with visible sternocleidomastoid lines. The bald head sits high on it, which increases the elongated look.
(7) Body fat: very low (about 6-8%). Veins show on the forearms and biceps.
(8) Posture at rest: upright and slightly loose. Shoulders relaxed and a little forward; arms hang with a slight bend. On defence he crouches deep with a wide stance.
In silhouette he reads as thinner and longer than LeBron and Giannis-level bulk, but more muscular through the chest and arms than Kyrie.
profiles.face:
Head: long, oval-to-slightly-egg-shaped cranium, made very prominent by the shaved head. The skull rises high above the ears with a smooth, rounded crown and a full, rounded occiput, so the back of the head bulges clearly in profile. From the front the head is narrower than it is tall: the face is long and lean, not wide.
Forehead: very high, smooth and gently domed (helped by the shaved scalp). There is a mild brow-ridge bulge, and the temples are slightly hollow.
Brows: dark, fairly thin, low, nearly straight, with a soft arch at the outer third. They sit close above the eyes, which gives him an intense, slightly hooded look.
Eyes: dark brown (almost black iris, #2A1A12), almond-shaped and medium-small. The upper lids are heavy and hooded, so the visible lid is narrow. The outer corners are level to slightly downturned. Spacing is normal to slightly wide. Faint under-eye bags and creases appear in the 1997-98 era.
Nose: broad, especially at the alar base (wide, flared nostrils); the nostrils are visible from the front. The bridge is low-to-moderate and straight, with no hump. The tip is rounded and fleshy, and the nose is medium-long.
Mouth: wide, with full lips. The lower lip is fuller and slightly everted. The upper lip is partly framed by the moustache, and there is mild forward projection of the mouth area. At rest the mouth is closed and neutral to slightly pursed, often chewing gum. When he smiles, it is a broad, toothy grin with a gap-free upper row.
Jaw and chin: a long lower face. The jawline is defined and angular but not wide. The chin is rounded, moderately prominent and slightly long, with the goatee sitting on it.
Cheekbones: high and visible, with lean, slightly hollow cheeks below. There are noticeable nasolabial lines when he talks or smiles.
Ears: a key likeness cue. They are large, taller than average, and stand clearly out from the bald head (cup-protrusion about 25-30 degrees). The helix rim is rounded, the lobes are fleshy and attached-to-free, and they sit at normal height. With the shaved head they are one of the first things you notice from the front.
Expressions on court: (a) a calm, almost bored game face with eyes narrowed; (b) tongue hanging out, slightly to one side, during drives and dunks; (c) a snarling, mouth-open scream after big plays; (d) a smirk or "I can't help it" shrug grin; (e) lips pressed together and jaw set at the free-throw line.
profiles.hair:
Fully shaved, shiny bald head (0 mm of hair; render as smooth skin with an extra specular/clearcoat sheen and faint stubble shadow under about 0.5 mm only at the sides and back near the old hairline, using a slightly darker multiply at about 10-15% opacity). The old hairline is irrelevant because he is bald. He has no sideburns. Eyelashes are short and dark. The eyebrows are covered in the face description (thin, dark, low).
Alternate 1984-88 skin only: very short, close-cropped tight curls about 3-5 mm long, colour #120C0A, with a receding hairline that has deep temple recessions and a peak.
profiles.facialHair:
1995-98 look:
(1) Moustache: a thin, neat, closely trimmed moustache about 2-4 mm long. It covers the upper-lip skin as a band roughly 6-9 mm tall at the centre, tapering at the mouth corners. It does not hang over the lip line and is denser at the centre than at the ends.
(2) Goatee: a small, short chin goatee/soul patch about 2-4 mm long. It covers the front of the chin about 3 cm wide and 2.5 cm tall, plus a thin patch directly under the lower lip.
(3) Linking lines: very faint, sparse lines run from the moustache ends down past the mouth corners to the chin patch. At gameplay distance treat it as a light "circle beard" ring, about 35-45% opacity on the sides and 80-90% at the moustache centre and chin.
(4) Cheeks and jawline: clean-shaven, with no beard on the cheeks or jaw.
Colour: black #0E0A09.
Implementation: use a darkened, slightly roughened skin decal (alpha mask) instead of strand geometry. In close-ups, add a short card-hair or normal-map stipple.
Alternate: the 1991-93 look is moustache-only and thinner, with a very faint chin patch. The rookie skin had a thin moustache and no goatee.
profiles.accessories:
(1) Wristband: one wristband, colour matched to the uniform (red on the red road kit, black on the black alternate, white on the white home kit). It is worn on the LEFT arm and usually pushed well up the forearm, about 6-10 cm below the elbow, not at the wrist. In some games it sits at the wrist, so the default is mid-forearm. It is about 9 cm wide and terry-towel textured. The right arm stays bare (shooting arm).
(2) Shorts: long and baggy for the time, with the hem about 2-4 cm above the top of the kneecap and a loose, wide leg. A short (about 1-2 cm) light-blue undershort hem can peek out as an easter egg (he wore his old college shorts under his uniform). This is optional and colour only, with no logo.
(3) Jersey: loose fit, tank top with wide armholes, tucked in.
(4) Socks: low-to-mid crew socks, white with the white kit or black with the black kit, showing about 6-10 cm above the shoe. The 1998 Finals look was low black socks with black shoes.
(5) Shoes: mid/high-top basketball shoes with no logos. Colourway A ('Concord'-like, home): white upper, glossy black patent-leather mudguard wrapping the lower half, translucent icy-blue/clear outsole. Colourway B ('Bred'-like, road): black mesh upper, black patent mudguard, red outsole. Alternate ('Flu Game'-like): black upper with red accents.
(6) No headband, no arm sleeve, no finger tape, no knee pads, no visible jewellery on court (he sometimes wore a small earring off court; omit it).
(7) Mouth: often chewing gum, so an idle jaw chew animation is a plus.

signatureMoves: TURNAROUND FADEAWAY JUMPER (right-handed, from the left mid-post or the baseline; the 1998 Last Shot is the same family). Timings are at 30 fps from the catch or the last dribble. Fr 0-6, setup: back to basket, feet shoulder-width plus a bit (about 0.55 m), knees flexed about 45 deg, pelvis lowered about 12 cm, spine01-03 flexed forward about 20 deg in total. Ball held at the right hip in both hands with elbows out (chinned). Head turned about 30 deg over the right shoulder to read the defender. Fr 6-10, optional shoulder fake: pelvis and spine yaw 15 deg to the left (middle) while the head stays toward the baseline, then snap back; ball moves 10 cm left with the shoulders. Fr 10-18, pivot: the left foot is the pivot; rotate it on the ball of the foot about 180 deg toward the baseline/right, while the right foot swings around and plants about 0.5 m away, so the player now squares to the rim, chest at 70-80 deg toward the basket. Pelvis drops another 5 cm to load, and the ball rises from the hip to the chin in both hands. Fr 18-22, take-off: both feet push off, but the body drifts BACKWARD about 0.4-0.7 m away from the rim/defender over the jump. Pelvis travels backward and up, the spine extends and then leans back 12-18 deg from vertical, and the head stays level, eyes on the rim. Fr 20-26, shooting motion: ball moves to the set point just above and in front of the right eye/forehead. Right upper arm is raised about 100-110 deg; right elbow is under the ball and slightly out about 5-10 deg; right hand is under the ball with fingers spread and the wrist cocked back about 70 deg. Left (guide) hand is on the left side of the ball, fingers up. Fr 24-28, airborne knee kick: the right thigh flexes 35-45 deg and the knee comes up while the left leg hangs straighter (the scissor-split that is his trademark). Toes point down. Fr 26-30, release at the APEX, about 55-70 cm jump: right elbow extends fully, the forearm sweeps up to about 60-70 deg above horizontal, and the wrist snaps forward/down 90 deg so the fingers point at the floor and slightly toward the rim. The guide hand leaves the ball sideways, opening out about 15 cm with no push. Ball launch at about 48-52 deg arc with backspin about 2 rev/s. Fr 30-42, hold the follow-through: the right arm stays extended with the wrist limp (goose neck) during the descent; the left arm drops to shoulder height. The 'Last Shot' variant holds the pose about 1 s after landing, both feet together, slight backward lean. Land on both feet about 0.5 m behind the take-off spot, knees absorbing 30 deg.

1988 FREE-THROW-LINE DUNK (stylised; used for breakaway or showtime dunk replays). Approach: full-speed run with the ball in the right hand. The final gather 2-3 m before the free-throw line is a long stride with the ball pulled into both hands at the right hip. Penultimate step (right foot, fr 0-6): long step, centre of mass lowered about 15 cm, trunk leaning back about 10 deg to convert speed. Plant (left foot, fr 6-10): one-foot take-off from the LEFT foot exactly at the free-throw line, 4.6 m from the rim. The left knee extends hard (about 120 to 175 deg) while the right thigh drives up to horizontal, and the ball rises to chest height in both hands. Flight (fr 10-36, about 0.85 s total hang in game; slow-mo replay at 0.35x): the legs open into a wide scissor split, the hallmark Jumpman silhouette. The left (take-off) leg trails behind and below, nearly straight, toe pointed. The right leg is flexed and swung forward with the knee about 90 deg at hip height, then extends forward as he approaches the rim. Fr 14-24, double clutch: the ball is brought down to the waist (both hands), then the right hand alone sweeps it back and up. The right upper arm circles from 0 deg to about 170 deg of flexion, the elbow is bent about 90 deg so the ball cocks behind the right ear/head, and the left arm extends forward/up toward the rim for balance. The torso arches back about 15 deg, the head tilts up, and the TONGUE IS OUT (jaw open about 20 deg, tongue extended about 3 cm and drooping slightly left). Fr 26-32, finish: the right arm whips forward over the top (tomahawk): shoulder flexion goes from 170 to 130 deg, the elbow extends and the wrist snaps, and the ball is jammed down through the rim. The right hand grips the rim for about 6 frames (optional), the legs come together, and he drops. Land on both feet under the rim, knees flexed 60 deg; then a one-step jog-out with a clenched-fist celebration. Ball path: hip, chest, waist (clutch), behind head, rim; peak hand height about 3.5 m.

THE MOVE (1991 Finals, mid-air hand switch to a left-hand reverse layup). Right-handed drive from the right wing toward the middle of the lane. Last dribble with the right hand, then a gather into the right hand only, cupped against the right forearm (big-hand palm). Two-foot or left-foot take-off about 2 m from the rim, initially rising as if to dunk with the right hand: the right arm is raised overhead, ball cocked at about 160 deg of shoulder flexion, and the tongue is out. Fr 8-14 (rising): the defender's arm appears in front, so he pulls the ball DOWN. The right arm sweeps down and in to the belly while the torso pikes forward 20 deg and both knees tuck 70 deg. Fr 14-20 (apex/drift): the body drifts right past the rim plane, and the ball passes from the right hand to the left hand in front of the belly. The left hand palms the ball, and the right hand goes up/out to shield (elbow 90 deg). Fr 20-28 (descent): the left arm extends out and up to the left, shoulder abducted about 110 deg; the wrist flicks with English and the ball is kissed high off the glass on the RIGHT side of the backboard to drop in. Head turns up-left to watch, spine side-bends about 15 deg to the left. Land on both feet beyond the rim on the right side and keep running out of bounds.

ROCK-THE-CRADLE DUNK (breakaway, 1990s game version of his 1985-87 dunks). Two-hand gather, then the ball is cupped in the RIGHT hand pressed against the inside of the right forearm (the 'cradle'). Take-off from two feet (or the left foot) about 1.2 m from the rim. Fr 4-10: the right arm swings the ball DOWN and BACK in an arc. Shoulder extension goes to about -30 deg (ball beside the right hip/thigh), the elbow is slightly bent, and the trunk flexes forward 10 deg. Fr 10-18: the arm swings forward and up in a big pendulum (shoulder flexion from -30 to about 175 deg) while the knees tuck. Fr 18-22: the right hand throws the ball down through the rim; the wrist flexes 80 deg. The left arm is out to the side for balance throughout. Tongue out. Optional rim hang for 4 frames.

JAB STEP INTO PULL-UP (triple threat, right or left elbow). Fr 0-8: triple-threat stance, ball at the right hip, knees flexed 50 deg, weight 60% on the left (pivot) foot. Fr 8-14: a hard, short jab with the right foot about 35 cm toward the defender's left hip (outward); shoulders and head dip 10 cm and the ball sweeps low across to the left knee. Fr 14-18: if the defender bails out, the right foot returns beside the left, the ball swings up to the set point, and he goes into the standard jumper (straight up, about 50 cm). If the defender stays, he rip-throughs: the ball swings low from the left knee to the right hip, then takes one hard right dribble and drives. He disguises it with a head-and-ball pump fake (ball rises to forehead height, eyes on the rim, heels stay down) about 40% of the time before the jab.

PULL-UP JUMPER OFF THE DRIBBLE (left elbow, going right). Two hard right-hand dribbles. On the last one he stops with a 1-2 step (left foot then right foot) or a hop stop. He picks the ball up at the right hip, rises straight up (minimal fade, about 10-20 cm), and takes it to the forehead set point. Release at the apex at about 50-60 cm, with the same right-hand mechanics as the fadeaway but no leg split: knees together, toes pointed down. Hold the follow-through.

DEFENSIVE STANCE AND STEAL (on-ball). Very low stance: feet about 0.8 m apart, knees flexed 70 deg, pelvis about 25 cm lower than standing, back flat and inclined about 30 deg. Both arms wide and active: the right hand low, mirroring the ball; the left hand high to deny the pass. He slides with quick shuffle steps, without crossing his feet. Steal swipe: an upward swipe (right hand from knee to waist) at the ball on the dribble's way up, then he immediately runs out, often finishing alone. Occasionally slaps both palms on the floor before a key defensive possession (an echo of his teammates in the 1990s); optional.
profiles.shootingForm:
Right-handed. Compact, repeatable one-motion jumper that is high and quick.
Set point: just above and in front of the right side of the forehead (ball centre about 10-15 cm above the eyebrows). It is not far behind the head.
Release: at or just before the apex of the jump, very high: hand at about 3.0 m on a jumper, so it is hard to block.
Shooting elbow: under the ball, with a slight outward flare of 5-10 deg. The upper arm is about 100-110 deg from the torso at set.
Guide hand: on the left side, with fingers pointing up. It comes off cleanly and opens to the side at release, with no thumb flick.
Follow-through: full elbow extension, a strong wrist snap with fingers pointing at the floor (goose neck). On big shots he holds it through the landing; the 1998 Last Shot pose is held about 1 s.
Arc: medium-high, about 48-52 deg.
Jump height: about 50-60 cm on pull-ups, about 55-70 cm on fadeaways. He gets more lift than most shooters.
Fade: about 0.4-0.7 m backward on turnaround fadeaways, with the trademark leg kick/split (one knee raised) as he drifts. A one-legged fade off the right foot appears late in his career (1996-98), with the left knee up. Straight up on catch-and-shoot threes, which are slightly flatter and less smooth.
Quirks: shoulders square early on the turnaround; tongue usually in on jumpers (out on drives); very quick gather-to-release (about 0.45 s off the catch).
Free-throw routine: toes on the line, right foot slightly forward. Three dribbles, a spin of the ball in his hands to find the seams, a deep knee bend (about 70 deg) and a fluid single-motion shot. Easter egg: 1991 eyes-closed free throw (eyelids shut, head level).
mannerisms: Tongue out: mouth open, tongue extended about 2-4 cm and drooping slightly to his left, on drives, layups and every dunk (start at the gather, retract on landing). This is the most iconic facial cue; also use it in dunk replays.

The Shrug (1992 Finals): after a hot shooting streak, he jogs back on defence turning toward the sideline with both palms up and out at waist height, shoulders raised about 8 cm, head tilted, a slight 'I can't explain it' smile. Total about 1.2 s.
Clutch fist-pump celebration (1989 'The Shot'): leaps on the spot with a right-fist uppercut, punching the air 2-3 times while airborne; mouth open in a scream.
Last Shot hold: on a game winner, he holds the shooting follow-through (right arm up, wrist limp) for a beat after landing.
Resting on defence or in a dead ball: bent at the waist with both hands gripping the hem of his shorts above the knees, head down, chest heaving.
Chewing gum: a continuous slow jaw chew at idle (jaw rotate 3-5 deg at about 1.5 Hz).
Wiping the soles of his shoes with his palms before a big possession or free throw (lift the foot behind, hand swipes the sole, then the other foot).
Point and smirk: after a big play he points at the scorer's table or a teammate with the index finger, then a half-smile with closed lips.
Flu Game (1997): exhausted walk and slump with an arm over a teammate's shoulder; optional end-of-game animation when he has low stamina.
Free-throw line: three dribbles, a spin of the ball in his hands, a deep knee dip; occasional eyes-closed easter egg.
High-five habit: jogs past teammates slapping hands low, then claps once hard before setting on defence.
profiles.tendencies:
Role: alpha scoring wing and first option in the clutch. He takes the last shot about 85% of the time when the game is within 3 points in the final 24 s.
Shot mix (game AI weights): mid-range about 45% (elbow pull-ups, wing isos, baseline and post fadeaways), at-rim about 38% (drives, transition dunks, cuts), three-point about 10% (mostly catch-and-shoot from the wings or corners, plus late-clock pull-ups), free throws drawn very frequently (high foul-draw on drives).
Preferred spots: right elbow, left elbow, both mid-post blocks (the turnaround fadeaway toward the baseline is his go-to), and right-wing isolation.
Isolation logic: catch on the wing, triple threat, jab step or pump fake (40%), then drive if the defender bites, or pull up if the defender sags. He posts up smaller guards: back down 1-2 dribbles, then turnaround fadeaway (60%), up-and-under or spin baseline (25%), or a pass out to the open shooter if double-teamed (15%).
Drives: attacks going right a little more (60/40). Finishes with hang-time layups, hand switches and reverses over bigs, and a one-hand dunk when the lane is clear. In transition he dunks with high probability, with showtime dunks (cradle, tomahawk, the free-throw-line version on long breakaways) when the game is out of reach or the crowd meter is high.
Passing: a willing, smart passer within the triangle. He hits the cutter or the corner shooter when doubled and drives and kicks late. He is not a primary playmaker; he takes over when the team is cold.
Off-ball: curls off screens to the elbow, back-door cuts when he is denied, and offensive rebound put-backs from the wing.
Defence: elite on-ball perimeter defender who guards the opponent's best scorer (Kobe, Kyrie, LeBron in this roster). Low stance, ball pressure, swipes on the way up, and he jumps passing lanes (gambles about 1.3x the league default), leading to breakaway dunks. He helps from the weak side with chase-down/weak-side blocks at the rim. He avoids defending Yao in the post; switch him onto guards. Draws charges occasionally.
Clutch modifier: +6 to mid-range, +4 layup, +3 steal in the last 2 minutes of close games.
Fatigue: high stamina, but he shows the Flu Game slump animation below 15% stamina.

profiles.build: Built like a linebacker on a 2.06 m frame, and his silhouette is very different from a generic 1.98 m athlete. (1) Shoulders: very broad (biacromial width about 50-52 cm) with huge, rounded deltoids and high, thick trapezius muscles running into the neck, so the shoulder line looks almost horizontal and the neck seems short. (2) Chest: deep barrel chest with heavy, square pectorals. The torso is deep front-to-back, not just wide. The V-taper is clear but the waist is thick and solid, not wasp-thin: about 86-90 cm waist against roughly 125+ cm chest. (3) Back: wide lats that flare when his arms are raised. (4) Arms: long (wingspan about 2.14 m, about 6% more than his barefoot height), with heavy biceps and triceps and thick forearms and wrists. The arms hang slightly away from the torso because of the lats and deltoids. (5) Legs: powerful thighs and glutes and solid calves. His knees are not bony. For his height the legs are of normal length, and the torso is relatively long and massive, so the upper body dominates. (6) Neck: very thick (about 48-50 cm), blending into the traps. (7) Hands: large, about 24 cm span. (8) Low body fat (about 6-8%) but big muscle mass everywhere, so the overall impression is heavy and dense. On court he stands upright and chest-forward, and his stride is powerful and long.
profiles.face: Head shape: broad, square-to-rectangular head with a strong, wide mandible whose jaw angles are at the beard line. The head looks slightly small relative to the enormous shoulders and neck. Forehead: tall and broad, made to look even higher by the receding hairline, with a gently rounded forward curve, and the headband sits across its upper third. Brow: heavy, prominent supraorbital ridge. The eyebrows are thick, low and fairly straight, with slightly lowered outer ends, which gives him a serious, intense look. Eyes: dark brown (about #2B1A12), almond-shaped, deep-set under the brow and somewhat hooded with a heavy upper-lid fold. The opening is moderately narrow, with average spacing and slightly downturned outer corners. Slight under-eye fullness by 2016. Nose: broad and fairly long, with a medium-wide bridge, a wide rounded bulbous tip and wide, flared nostrils. The nostril width is about the inner-canthus distance or more. Lips: full upper and lower lips (the lower lip slightly fuller), a mouth of medium-wide width with a slight forward projection. Usually partly hidden by the moustache at the top. Jaw/chin: wide, strong chin of moderate height with a slight forward projection, fully covered by the beard. Cheekbones: moderately prominent, with lean cheeks below them because of low body fat. Ears: fairly small, sitting close to the head and slightly low, with modest lobes. Expression on court: neutral to stern, focused eyes and a slightly open mouth when breathing hard. Typical expressions are a wide-open roar with bared teeth after big plays (the lower jaw drops fully and the neck veins and traps tense), a puffed-cheek exhale, a calm 'chin-up' stare down, and a wide grin when laughing with teammates.
profiles.hair: Very short black buzz cut, about 3-5 mm, of uniform length, tightly coiled (texture shows as a dark matte stipple, not strands). The hairline is clearly receded: deep M-shaped temple recession and a thin frontal area, so the hair edge starts about 7-8 cm above the brow centre and further back at the temples. The headband covers most of the front hairline, and hair shows above the headband at the crown and sides. The sides and back are tapered short (2-3 mm), with a sharp lined-up edge around the ears and a neat, squared nape line. Colour: #141010 (near-black, no grey in 2016). Implementation: a dark matte scalp-hair shell or decal (opacity ~0.85) above the hairline mask, with the region from the forehead to the headband left as skin.
profiles.facialHair: Full, dense, connected beard, about 10-15 mm long on the chin and jaw and 6-10 mm on the cheeks, tightly coiled and near-black (#120E0C). The upper cheek line is crisp, sharply lined and fairly high: it runs straight from the sideburn, about 1 cm in front of the ear and level with the bottom of the ear tragus, diagonally down to roughly 1.5 cm outside the mouth corner. The beard is connected to a thick, full moustache that is trimmed at the upper-lip edge and covers the philtrum. The chin beard projects slightly forward and down, which makes the jaw look squarer and longer. Neckline: about 2-3 cm below the jaw, following the jaw curve; the throat is clean-shaven. Sideburns are full and blend into the beard and the short hair. Implementation: a beard shell on the lower face (offset 4-8 mm outward on the chin, 2-4 mm on the cheeks) with a noisy, alpha-dithered edge, and a darker skin-tone underlayer to fake density.
profiles.accessories: Headband: a plain terry headband (no logo), about 5 cm tall, worn level and high on the forehead so it covers the receding front hairline. Default black, white for the home-white kit. It is the most important accessory. Arms: no arm sleeve in this era. Optional: a black compression sleeve on the left arm, sometimes seen in other seasons. Wristbands: none by default. Fingers: no tape. Knee/leg: no knee pads; occasionally black knee-length compression tights under the shorts (optional variant). Socks: crew-to-mid-calf athletic socks, white with the white kit and black with the dark kit, pulled up to about 15 cm above the ankle bone. Shoes: bulky high-top basketball shoes, wine/gold/black or white/gold colourways, with a thick midsole and no logos. Jewellery: none on court. Tattoos (the colours are subtle on his dark skin, so render them as slightly darker, desaturated detail-map patches): 'CHOSEN 1' in arched Old-English lettering across the upper back between the shoulder blades, partly visible above the jersey's back neckline; dense tattoo coverage on both upper arms (a lion head on the right biceps/shoulder area) and on both forearms; a large chest piece (crest with lions, 'HISTORY'/'FAMILY' lettering) under the jersey. The visible arm tattoos help likeness in close-ups.
profiles.jersey: #23. Main kit (2016 dark/road): deep wine/burgundy body (#6F263D), gold numerals and trim (#FFB81C) outlined in navy (#041E42), gold/navy piping at the armholes and collar. The number is on both front and back. Alternate home kit: white body (#FFFFFF), wine numerals with gold outline and wine/gold trim. Shorts match the kit with side-panel trim, at knee length. Fallback alternates: #6 in black/red/white (Miami 2012-13 look) or #6/#23 in purple/gold (Lakers). Avoid them in a game that has Kobe in purple/gold and Jordan in red/black.
signatureMoves: CHASE-DOWN BLOCK (2016 Finals Game 7 version; total about 1.6 s at 30 fps, in a fast-break defensive state when the ball-handler has 1-2 m of separation; 48 frames). F0-F18 SPRINT: a full-speed run cycle about 1.25x faster than his normal sprint (stride about 2.4 m), torso pitched 20-25 deg forward from pelvis/spine01, head up and locked on the ball, arms pumping hard (upper arm swing +/-60 deg at the shoulder, elbows bent 90 deg). Root speed about 8.5-9 m/s, closing to the shooter's off-ball hip on the trailing side. F18-F22 PENULTIMATE + PLANT: a long penultimate step lowers the pelvis 12 cm and the torso straightens to about 5 deg forward. One-foot takeoff from the LEFT foot (the right knee drives upward). Block with the RIGHT hand. F22-F30 TAKEOFF/RISE: the left ankle, knee and hip extend explosively. The right thigh flexes to 100 deg (knee drive) and the right calf folds to 90 deg. The right arm swings from the hip straight up past the ear, with the shoulder (clavicle) elevated and upper arm abducted/flexed about 170 deg, elbow almost straight (10-15 deg), wrist extended, fingers spread. The left arm swings down and back for balance (shoulder extended 30 deg). Spine02/03 extend 10 deg back and the head tilts up 20 deg to watch the ball. Vertical rise about 0.85-0.9 m. Forward momentum continues (root still moving about 6 m/s, so the body flies past the shooter's back). F30-F33 CONTACT: at the apex the right hand comes from behind and above and slaps the ball flat against the backboard. The wrist flexes forward hard (from +40 extension to -20) and the forearm pronates. The ball path is pinned to the glass, held for 2 frames, then it drops off along the glass (or ricochets toward a teammate). Contact point: about 3.3-3.4 m above the floor, about 0.3 m right of the rim centre on the glass. F33-F42 FLY-THROUGH: the body continues out of bounds or under the baseline. The legs extend for landing, the right arm stays high with the fingers spread and then drops, and the torso rotates 20-30 deg toward the court to look back. F42-F48 LANDING: a two-foot or staggered landing with the knees flexing 45 deg and the pelvis dropping 15 cm, followed by 2 decelerating steps. Optional celebration: a stare back or a fist clench.

TOMAHAWK DUNK, right hand (transition, from a full sprint; about 1.3 s, 40 frames). F0-F10 APPROACH: dribble with the right hand in a speed-dribble stride, then pick up the ball off the last dribble at about 3.5 m from the rim. F10-F16 GATHER/LAST TWO STEPS: on the pickup the ball is taken with both hands into the right hip pocket. Step 1 (right foot) is long and step 2 (left foot) is a quick plant, giving a ONE-FOOT left-leg takeoff (a two-foot jump-stop variant is also common for him: both feet plant together, pelvis dropped 18 cm). The torso leans back 10 deg on the plant to convert speed into height. F16-F24 RISE + WIND-UP: the left leg drives up, with the right thigh flexed 90 deg and the knee leading. The ball is lifted in the right hand only. The right shoulder externally rotates and abducts so the ball is cocked BEHIND THE HEAD: upper arm about 160 deg flexion, elbow flexed 100-120 deg, ball about 25 cm behind the occiput, wrist cupping the ball (extended 40 deg). The left arm reaches forward and up toward the rim for balance (shoulder 120 deg flexion, elbow 20 deg). The spine arches back 15-20 deg (spine02/03 extension) and the head and chin come up. Rise about 0.85 m, and the head ends level with or above the rim. F24-F28 HAMMER: the right arm whips forward and down in a big arc. The elbow extends quickly, the shoulder flexes forward, the wrist snaps from 40 extension to 40 flexion, and the spine flexes forward 25 deg (crunch). The ball travels in an arc from behind the head down through the rim, released or slammed at about 0.25 m above the rim, going straight down. F28-F32 RIM: the right hand grabs the front of the rim for 3-6 frames with the fingers curled, and the body swings slightly forward under the rim with the knees tucked. F32-F40 LANDING + ROAR: he releases the rim and lands on two feet with the knees bent 50 deg and a wide stance, then goes into the 'roar' (jaw fully open, chest out, arms flexed down and out with fists clenched at hip level, spine03 extended, head up and slightly back). Total ball path: hip, then behind the head, then down through the rim.

POWER DRIVE ('bulldozer' attack from the top or wing; about 1.2 s to the finish). F0-F6 JAB/HESITATION: from triple threat or a live dribble, a quick jab or hesitation with the lead foot as the shoulders feint 10 deg the other way. F6-F14 FIRST STEP: a long, low first step (2.0 m+) going right or left (he is comfortable both ways; slight preference for driving left and finishing with the right hand across, or left-handed at the rim). The pelvis drops 15 cm, the torso pitches 30-35 deg forward with a straight spine, and the ball is pounded hard and low (bounce at knee height) with the outside hand, kept on his hip away from the defender. F14-F24 SHOULDER BUMP: on the 2nd-3rd dribble he lowers his inside shoulder into the defender's chest. The clavicle and upper arm on the inside side are protracted and the inside arm is a 'chicken wing' (elbow flexed 90 deg, upper arm abducted 45 deg) acting as a shield. On contact the defender is displaced 0.3-0.6 m, while LeBron's path deflects less than 10 deg (strength advantage). F24-F30 GATHER: a big two-hand gather into the chest/hip on a long step, usually ending in a TWO-FOOT JUMP-STOP 1.2-1.8 m from the rim with the pelvis dropping 20 cm and the ball high and protected under the chin. F30-F40 FINISH: either (a) a two-hand power dunk (both arms lifting the ball from the chin straight up over the head and slamming down, with the spine flexing 20 deg on the slam); (b) a strong one-hand layup off the glass at the top of the jump, with the off arm extended toward the defender to create space (not a push); or (c) a 'kick-out' if help collapses (see passing tendencies). Finishes through contact: and-one animation is a flexing roar.

CROSS-COURT ONE-HAND SKIP PASS / NO-LOOK (his signature playmaking). From a drive at the elbow or the baseline, while his head and eyes stay toward the rim or the defender, plant the inside foot. The ball is pulled with the right hand from the dribble up to shoulder height in one motion with the wrist cocked back. Then the arm whips across the body: the shoulder adducts across the chest, the forearm extends, the wrist snaps and the fingers follow through toward the target corner. The torso rotates only 15-20 deg (the head does NOT turn). Ball path: a fast, near-flat line drive about 1.8-2.4 m high, travelling across the court in 0.5-0.7 s to the shooter's shooting pocket. Variant: a two-handed overhead skip pass from the post (arms straight overhead, elbows 15 deg, a snap from both wrists).

LEFT-BLOCK FADEAWAY (Miami 2012-13 / Cleveland post game). He posts on the left block with his back to the basket, receives the ball in both hands at the chest with a wide stance (feet 0.8 m apart, pelvis dropped 15 cm), and backs down with 1-2 power dribbles (right hand) as his left elbow and forearm hold the defender off. He turns over the right shoulder (a reverse pivot on the left foot of about 150 deg) and faces the basket. Then he shoots a fadeaway: the jump goes up and 0.4-0.5 m backward, the torso leans back 15-20 deg, the legs split slightly forward (the right knee kicks forward 30 deg), and the set point is above and slightly in front of the forehead with a high release. A face-up jab-and-shoot is a variant.

PULL-UP / STEP-BACK THREE (secondary). On a left-to-right crossover at the top, one hard dribble going right, then a quick step-back off the right foot, landing on two feet balanced 0.5 m behind his original spot. The shot goes up in one motion with a slight fade, a fast release and a big follow-through held for about 10 frames.
profiles.shootingForm: Right-handed jump shot (he is naturally left-handed in daily life but shoots right-handed). Stance: feet about shoulder width apart with the right foot slightly ahead, toes angled about 10-15 deg left of the rim, knees bent 40-50 deg. Dip/load: the ball starts at hip or waist height and comes up in a near one-motion lift along the right side of the body. Set point: in front of and slightly above the forehead, a bit right of the head's centre line, with the ball about 15-20 cm in front of the face. Elbow: slightly flared out (about 10-15 deg off vertical), not tucked. Guide hand: on the left side of the ball with the thumb pointing back, and it comes off cleanly at release. In his early years his guide-hand thumb sometimes pushed the ball slightly (a historical quirk). Release: slightly before the apex of the jump, at a release height of about 2.8-2.9 m on jumpers. Jump height: modest on set shots (15-25 cm), with more lift on pull-ups. Fade: little on catch-and-shoot threes, a clear backward lean (10-20 deg) on deep or step-back threes and on post fadeaways, often with a slight right-leg kick forward. Follow-through: full elbow extension, a firm wrist snap with the fingers pointed at the rim, held for about 0.3 s. Arc: medium-flat (launch angle about 44-46 deg). Free throws: the same mechanics with a small dip and no jump (heels rise). Quirks: on a miss he sometimes shuffles slightly backward, and he has a 'hold the pose' follow-through on makes in big moments.
mannerisms: CHALK TOSS (pregame or team intro): walks to the scorer's table, rubs powder or chalk between both hands (palms together, 4-5 rubbing strokes of about 0.6 s), turns toward the crowd, spreads his arms and claps them upward. Both arms sweep from waist height to straight overhead (shoulders 170 deg flexion, elbows nearly straight), the hands fling apart, and a white powder cloud (particle burst about 1.5 m in diameter, drifting up and outward over 1.5 s) rises over his head. The head tilts back 20 deg and the chest puffs out. Great for intro and menu animations.
Headband adjust: with both hands, index and middle fingers push the headband up or down, about 0.5 s. Do it during dead balls and before free throws.

Primal roar after a dunk or an and-one: the jaw opens fully with bared teeth, the neck tenses, both arms are flexed down at his sides with fists clenched (a 'Hulk' flex), the chest pushes forward, and he often stomps or stares at the crowd. Sometimes he slaps or pounds his chest twice with his right fist.
Silencer / finger-to-lips (later eras) and 'too strong' biceps flex: right arm curled up, left hand slapping the biceps.
Pointing: points to the passer after an assist made to him, or two fingers to the sky after big plays.
Idle: hands on his knees and breathing heavily during free throws, a slight sway, and he chews on or bites his fingernails on the bench. He also stands with hands on hips, chest out and elbows wide.

Free-throw routine: steps to the line and toes it with the right foot slightly ahead, takes the ball and spins it backward in his hands, takes 3 quick dribbles, a small shoulder shimmy and roll, a deep exhale through puffed cheeks, sets and shoots. After makes he gives a quick fist pump or claps once.
Pre-game and huddle: elaborate personal handshakes with each teammate (multi-step slaps, a hip bump, a 'shoot the arrow' gesture). A scaled-down 2-3 beat version can be used for team intros.
Expression: a stern neutral face in play, a wide smile when joking, an exaggerated incredulous face with both palms up to the referee after a no-call.
profiles.tendencies: An all-around point-forward. He brings the ball up himself and initiates from the top of the key or the right wing, about 60% of possessions as primary handler. Shot mix: drives to the rim are his first option (about 45%), then kick-outs or skip passes to shooters off his drives (high assist chance, the best passer among the six), then mid-range pull-ups from the elbows (about 15%), above-the-break threes (about 20%, more from the top and the left wing, often as pull-ups when a defender sags), and left-block post-ups or face-ups against smaller defenders (about 10%). He punishes mismatches: if guarded by a smaller player (Kyrie), back down and bully; if guarded by a bigger, slower player (Yao), face up and drive past. In transition he always pushes and goes all the way to the rim (tomahawk or two-hand dunk). On drives he jump-stops on two feet and makes the right read, passing out if two defenders collapse. He also uses the hit-ahead pass in transition and the cross-court skip. Rebounding: he crashes the defensive glass and leads the break himself. Defence: a versatile help defender who switches onto anyone (a 1-5 switchable feel). On the ball he plays strong, chesting up and walling off drives. Off the ball he gambles on passing lanes now and then (steal attempts) and, most of all, trails fast breaks to attempt the chase-down block from behind (trigger: an opponent breakaway layup when LeBron is within about 4 m behind and has sprint stamina, with a high success weight). In the clutch he takes the last shot, raises his drive and pass ratio and, in a tie game, looks for a drive and kick or a two-foot finish.

likenessPriorities: Silhouette and mass: a hulking, 113 kg linebacker frame on a 2.06 m body. Very wide boulder shoulders, a thick trap-and-neck block, a deep barrel chest, heavy arms hanging away from the torso and an upright chest-out posture. At about 120 px this is what tells LeBron apart from Giannis (longer and leaner), Jordan or Kobe (slimmer guards) and Yao (taller and narrower).

Headband plus hairline: a black (or white) headband worn high and level across the forehead, with a receded hairline and a very short near-black buzz cut showing above it. It is the strongest single signifier at gameplay distance.

Full dense black beard: crisp high cheek lines, a thick connected moustache and a squared chin beard that makes the jaw look wide and square. It contrasts with Jordan's bald head and goatee, Kobe's clean shave and Kyrie's thinner beard.
Kit and number: wine/burgundy jersey with gold #23 and navy outline (or white with wine/gold), plus dark tattoo-covered arms. Together with the headband this is the instant broadcast read.

Face in close-up: heavy straight brow over deep-set hooded intense dark eyes, a broad long nose with wide flared nostrils and a rounded tip, a full lower lip and a broad square face. Expressions include the open-mouth roar and the chalk toss in menus and replays.

profiles.era: 2020-21 season through the 2021 Finals (age 26). Back-to-back MVP (2019, 2020) leading into the title and Finals MVP run, including the 50-point closeout in Game 6. This is the most-replayed and most-merchandised version of him: green #34 icon jersey, short tight haircut with a sharp edge-up, short full beard, peak post-2017 muscle mass on a long, lean frame. The rookie look (shaved head, ~95 kg, beanpole) and the 2023+ shaved-head look are less recognisable as "Giannis".
