profiles.build: Long, lean and muscular, with a pronounced V-taper. Height 2.11 m in shoes (about 2.08-2.09 barefoot), 110 kg (BMI about 24.7). Compared with a generic 1.98 m athlete scaled up: (1) Arms are clearly longer. Ape index is +10 cm (wingspan/height 1.048), with most of the extra length in the forearm and a long hand, so hanging fingertips reach about mid-thigh, roughly 5 cm lower than average. (2) Hands are huge, about 25 cm long with a 30.5 cm span, so a basketball looks like a grapefruit in one palm. Make this visible in close-ups. (3) Torso is short relative to his legs and the legs are long, especially the shins, so the knee sits high. Nape-to-waist is short and the waist is high and narrow. (4) Shoulders are broad, square and high, with wide clavicles. The deltoids and trapezius are well developed (he added about 15 kg of muscle after 2013), but the chest is flat and modest rather than barrel-like. The lats are wide, giving a clear V. (5) Waist and hips are very narrow, the abdomen is flat, and the buttocks are small. (6) Thighs are strong but long and not bulky. Calves are long and slim with high muscle bellies; knees and ankles are bony and thin. (7) Neck is long, sinewy and moderately thick, with a visible Adam's apple. (8) The head is small for the body, about 8.5 head-heights in total. That makes him look even taller than 2.11 m and is a key silhouette cue. (9) Feet are long (US size about 16). (10) Posture: slight forward head carriage; at rest the shoulders roll forward a little and the long arms hang slightly in front of the thighs. Body fat is very low and veins show on the forearms and biceps.
profiles.face: Skin is deep warm brown with a reddish-brown undertone. Use about #523326 as the base, #6A4432 for highlights on the forehead, cheekbones and nose bridge, #3A2219 in shadow, slight sheen under arena lights, and a sweat specular layer. Head: long and relatively narrow, an oval-to-rectangular (egg) shape with a tall crown and a flat-ish back. The face is long, with a long lower third. Forehead: high and broad with a straight, slightly high hairline; gently sloped with a soft frontal bulge. Brow: a prominent brow ridge with dark, fairly thick, straight eyebrows sitting low over the eyes. The outer ends angle slightly down, which gives an intense, focused look in game. Eyes: deep-set beneath the brow, medium-small, almond-shaped and dark brown (near-black iris, #2B1A12). Spacing is average to slightly wide. The upper lids are slightly heavy and the lower lids show faint bags and fine creases. Wide-eyed with a lot of visible white when he roars. Nose: long, with a straight bridge of moderate height (not flat) and no hump. The lower third is broad: wide rounded tip, strongly flared alae and wide, rounded nostrils. The tip points slightly downward. Lips: full and wide, with the lower lip fuller than the upper and an even, gently defined cupid's bow. The mouth is wide; when he smiles it is very broad and shows both rows of white teeth. Jaw and chin: long, angular, lean jaw with visible gonial angles. The chin is long and slightly prominent and squarish-rounded. Cheekbones: high and prominent, with hollow lean cheeks below them, which shows strongly in close-ups. Ears: fairly large, set at average height and noticeably protruding (they stick out from the short haircut). The lobes are attached-to-medium. Neck: long, with a visible Adam's apple. Expressions on court: (a) a neutral game face with a slightly furrowed brow, lips closed or slightly parted, and a long serious look; (b) after an and-one dunk, a full roar with the mouth wide open, teeth bared, brows down and neck tendons out; (c) off-play, a big toothy grin with crinkled eyes and raised cheeks; (d) at the free-throw line, eyes down and a slow visible chest breath.
profiles.hair: Black (#141110), tight-coiled short natural hair. 2020-21 cut: about 8-12 mm on top with an even, soft texture (a sponge/curl look, not long twists). The sides and back are a low taper/fade: about 3 mm above the ears, blending to about 1 mm at the nape and around the ears. A crisp edge-up: the frontline is straight and relatively high with defined temple corners, and the sideburns are squared and connect into the beard. The overall head silhouette stays close to the skull, adding only about 1 cm on top, so the head still reads small. Implementation: a shell/fin layer over the scalp vertex group with a noise-based coil normal map. On a phone at gameplay distance, a dark matte cap with a sharp hairline edge is enough. Avoid a shiny skull, because the hair is matte and dense.
profiles.facialHair: Short full beard, close-cropped (2020-21 look). Black. Jaw and chin: about 4-6 mm, densest on the chin and along the jawline, giving a slightly squared, defined lower jaw. The cheek line is low and clean-shaven above the jaw, angling from the sideburn down toward the mouth corners, so the upper cheeks are bare. The sideburns connect to the beard at about 3 mm. Moustache: thin to medium (about 3 mm), connecting to the chin beard at the mouth corners and leaving a clear gap under the nose at the philtrum edge. Under the lower lip there is a short soul-patch fill joining the chin beard. The neck is cleaned up under the jaw; the beard ends roughly at the jaw shadow line. Density reads as moderate: darker than stubble but skin shows through on the cheeks. Implementation: an alpha/density texture on the face UV (or a short shell), darkening the jaw/chin silhouette. At 120 px it only needs to read as a darker, squarer jaw outline.
profiles.accessories: Minimal. Era-accurate defaults: no headband and no arm sleeves on either arm, so his bare long arms are part of the look. No wristbands (occasionally a thin white one; treat as off by default). Light white finger/thumb tape is optional and rare. No visible jewellery during play (no chains or earrings in games). No visible mouthguard during play. Sometimes thin black compression shorts or tights just past the hem; default to none, or short black liners barely visible. Socks: crew to mid-calf (top about 20 cm above the ankle bone), plain white with the green icon jersey or plain green/black as an alternate; no logos. signatureMoves: EUROSTEP FROM THE 3-PT LINE (signature, right-handed, attacking from the right wing or top). 30 fps; rim at +Z; standing pelvis height 1.18 m after scaling. F0 (0.00 s): live dribble at the 3-pt arc (7.2 m from the rim) in triple-threat lean. pelvis 1.05 m; spine_01-03 flexed forward 8/8/6 deg; head counter-flexed so the eyes stay level; ball in hand_r at the right hip. F0-F6: one long push dribble with the right hand. upperarm_r extends forward 40 deg, lowerarm_r extends to 15 deg flexion, hand_r pushes the ball about 1.3 m ahead so it bounces at about 0.6 m height. Strides L-R are each about 1.7 m; arms counter-swing. F7-F10 (0.23-0.33 s), GATHER: the ball rises into both hands at right-hip height. hand_l crosses the body; fingers spread wide (index/middle/ring/pinky_01 about 10 deg, thumb_01 abducted 40 deg) because the huge hands make the gather one-palm-ish. The right foot lands (heel strike) about 5.2 m from the rim. That is step 1: 2.0 m long, angled 25 deg to HIS RIGHT (the fake direction). pelvis yaws 15 deg right and drops to 1.00 m; spine_02 side-bends right 10 deg; head and eyes turn right 20 deg to sell the fake. Ball held at the right hip, elbows out (upperarm_l/r abducted 35 deg) to protect. F11-F17: airborne float. thigh_r flexed 30 deg, calf_r bent 40 deg, thigh_l swinging forward. F18 (0.60 s), STEP 2: the left foot plants about 1.7 m forward and 1.2 m laterally to HIS LEFT, crossing past the defender's hip. thigh_l flexes 55 deg; calf_l knee bend 65 deg; foot_l is turned 20 deg toward the rim. pelvis drops to 0.92 m and yaws back to face the rim; spine_01-03 side-bend left 6/6/4 deg. The BALL SWINGS across the body in a low-to-high arc from the right hip to the left shoulder (path: hip, sternum, left shoulder, about 0.35 s), so the torso shields it. F18-F24, LOAD: calf_l and thigh_l compress; thigh_r drives up to 90 deg flexion with calf_r folded 100 deg (knee drive). upperarm_l and upperarm_r flex to 150 deg as the ball rises over the left shoulder toward the head. F25 (0.83 s): takeoff off the LEFT foot. ball_l and foot_l plantarflex 40 deg; spine extends to neutral. F25-F36: rising. The ball transfers to hand_r cocked above and behind the head (upperarm_r flexed 170 deg, lowerarm_r flexed 70 deg); hand_l releases and stays up as a guard arm. Peak at F36 (1.20 s): hand_r about 0.25 m above the rim (3.30 m). F36-F38: wrist snap-down dunk (lowerarm_r extends, hand_r flexes 60 deg). hand_r fingers hook the rim for 4-8 frames; legs swing forward with knees bent 70 deg. F44 release; land two-footed at F52 with knees at 50 deg. Variant: if the defender does not shift, step 2 continues straight and he finishes with a two-hand dunk off two feet (jump stop on step 2).

LONG-GATHER TWO-HAND POWER DUNK IN TRANSITION. One dribble from about half-court-plus, then gather at the free-throw line extended (about 5.2 m out). F0: last dribble with the right hand at full sprint (stride about 2.1 m; pelvis 1.08 m; spine forward 15 deg). F8: gather as the right foot strikes. The ball snaps to both hands at the right hip, then pulls up the midline to the chest. F8-F16: a long right-foot step (2.1 m) into a LEFT-foot plant (or a two-foot jump stop on a 1.5 m hop). Penultimate step lowers pelvis to 0.90 m with spine_01-03 flexed 10 deg total. F16-F20, takeoff: hips and knees extend explosively; arms swing the ball up the midline to overhead. F20-F30, cock: the ball goes BEHIND THE HEAD in both hands. upperarm_l/r flexed 175 deg; lowerarm_l/r flexed 100 deg so the ball sits behind the neck_01 level; spine_02 and spine_03 extend (arch) 12 deg each; head extended 10 deg; knees tuck (thigh_l/r flexed 70 deg, calf_l/r flexed 110 deg). F31-F34, throw-down (crunch): spine_01-03 flex forward 10/12/10 deg; arms whip forward and down so the ball goes through the rim at peak, hands about 0.30 m above the rim. F34-F44: both hands grip the rim (hand_l and hand_r fingers fully curled). Body hangs; elbows bend 30 deg in a slight pull-up; legs swing forward, then knees lift up and apart (thigh_l/r flexed 60 deg, abducted 15 deg). F44: release, then a two-foot landing at F52 under the rim; immediately chains into the FLEX-AND-ROAR celebration. Variant: a one-hand right tomahawk where hand_r takes the ball in a wide circle behind the head (upperarm_r circumducts from 90 deg abduction to 180 deg flexion) and slams down.

REVERSE SPIN GATHER INTO THE LANE (from the right elbow or wing, cut off on a right-hand drive). F0-F6: driving right (toward the baseline) with right-hand dribbles; defender cuts off ahead-right. F7: hard plant of the LEFT foot, toes about 30 deg to the right of travel; pelvis 0.98 m; ball picked up with both hands at the right hip as the gather, so the spin is part of the two steps. F7-F19, spin: reverse pivot COUNTER-CLOCKWISE (viewed from above) on ball_l/foot_l, about 300 deg total over 0.4 s. Rotation leads with pelvis yaw, followed by spine_03 and head (whip the head around first at F10 to spot the rim). The right leg swings around with thigh_r abducted 30 deg and the knee bent 70 deg, and the right foot lands at F19 about 1.4 m past the defender's hip toward the rim. Ball kept tight at the right hip, elbows flared (upperarm abducted 40 deg) and right shoulder sealing the defender. F19-F24: load on the right foot and drive the left knee up. F25: takeoff off the RIGHT foot for a left-hand finish (or a two-foot jump stop for a two-hand dunk/layup). The ball rises up the left side with lowerarm_l extending; finger roll or flush at about 3.25 m. Landing at F40.

CHASE-DOWN / HELP BLOCK (2021 Finals G4 style). Approach: sprint from the weak side, 2.2 m strides, arms pumping. Two strides out: stutter to a left-foot penultimate step with pelvis 0.95 m. Takeoff off the LEFT foot (one foot) at F0. The inside arm (the hand nearer the ball, either side) extends straight up: upperarm flexed 175 deg, lowerarm fully extended, hand open with fingers spread and slightly hyperextended, the palm turned toward the ball. The other arm swings down and back for balance (upperarm extended 20 deg, abducted 40 deg). spine_02/03 lean 15 deg toward the ball; head up, eyes on the ball. The high hand peaks about 3.6 m at F12 and contacts the ball against the glass or rim with a downward-forward wrist flex of 40 deg (pin rather than swat). Then the body drifts past the rim; legs split (thigh_r flexed 80 deg, thigh_l extended 10 deg). Land on the left foot at F26, then the right; often followed by a roar with fists clenched.

POST/ELBOW FACE-UP DRIVE WITH A LONG STRIDE (the 'one dribble from the elbow to the rim' variant used as a quick move). Face up at the right elbow (about 4.5 m). Jab with the right foot 0.4 m (F0-F6, pelvis drop 5 cm, head fake right 10 deg). One left-hand crossover dribble while the left foot strides 1.9 m past the defender's left hip (F7-F15), with the ball going across from hand_r to hand_l at knee height. Gather on the left foot, then one more 1.8 m right-foot step (F16-F25), and a two-foot or one-foot (right) takeoff with a left-hand or two-hand finish. Use this as the default 'drive' when the AI is cut off at the elbow.
profiles.shootingForm: The jumper is functional but clearly worse than the legends' jumpers, and it should look slightly mechanical. Stance: feet shoulder-width, right foot about 10 cm ahead, toes turned about 10 deg left; knees flexed 35 deg in the dip. Dip: the ball drops to the waist or belt in both hands (a deep dip that adds time). Lift: the ball comes up the right side of the face. Set point: LOW for his height, at the forehead or just above the right eye (hand_r about 2.15-2.20 m from the floor while standing). Shooting elbow: right elbow flares out about 15-20 deg from vertical. Guide hand: hand_l on the left side of the ball, thumb up, with no push. Quirk: a short hitch or pause at the set point (3-5 frames) before the push, and the release often happens slightly on the way up rather than at the apex. Release height is about 2.90 m on jumpers. Jump height: low on threes (10-15 cm, almost a set shot) and about 25 cm on mid-range pull-ups, with a slight forward drift/kick of 10-20 cm. Follow-through: lowerarm_r fully extended about 45 deg above horizontal, wrist snapped, fingers pointing down, held for about 0.4 s; the guide hand pops off to the side. Arc: moderate-to-flat (entry about 42-44 deg). Misses tend to clank front-rim or back-rim hard. Free throw: same mechanics with no jump. A slow, deliberate dip to the waist and a noticeable pause at the set point; the push looks stiff and occasionally the knees and arms are out of sync (deliberately). Arc is flat. Career FT% is about 0.70, and in the 2021 era closer to 0.60-0.69. Driving finishes use the off-hand comfortably (left-hand finger rolls) and he very rarely shoots floaters.
mannerisms: FLEX-AND-ROAR after an and-one or power dunk. He lands, plants both feet wide (1 m apart) and bends the knees 20 deg. Both arms go into a double-biceps flex: upperarm_l/r abducted 90 deg, lowerarm_l/r flexed 110 deg, fists clenched. The torso leans forward 15 deg toward the crowd or camera, the mouth opens wide in a roar with teeth bared, brows down and neck tendons out. Hold 0.6-0.8 s, then two short downward fist pumps.
Chest thump after a big play: two quick right-fist hits to the left pec, then he points at a teammate.
Big toothy grin (crinkled eyes, very wide mouth) during dead balls, the bench interaction and the menu card; it contrasts with his intense game face.

FREE-THROW ROUTINE (long, famous; about 10-14 s in the 2021 era). (1) Receives the ball and walks to the line with eyes down. (2) Holds the ball low against the right hip in his right hand for about 5-6 s while taking a deep, visible breath with chest rise and shoulders lifting about 2 cm. (3) Brings the ball in front with both hands and spins it backward in his hands once. (4) One dribble, then catch. (5) A second breath. (6) Dip to the waist, slow rise, short pause at the set point, shoot. Crowds famously count out loud. In-game, cap the routine at 9 s (he was called for 10-second violations in 2021-22).
Idle stance: hands on hips with long fingers spread over the hip bones; torso slightly forward; head nods while listening. Between plays he bounces lightly on his toes and does shoulder rolls.
Wipes his face or beard with the bottom of the jersey or the back of his hand during stoppages; tugs the jersey neckline.
Defensive stance: very wide, low and long. Arms spread at shoulder height in a 2.2 m 'wall' with hands open and fingers spread. He shuffles with long, low slides.
After a made shot in transition he backpedals with the right index finger raised or both arms out like an airplane (light celebration).
Hangs on the rim after dunks with knees pulled up, then lets go; a slight swing forward.
profiles.tendencies: An attack-the-rim slasher and transition freight train. Shot mix: about 60% at the rim (dunks and layups), 15% short paint, 10% mid-range (mostly elbow face-ups), and 15% above-the-break threes. He takes threes only when wide open (defender more than 2.5 m away, usually because the defence is sagging in drop coverage). There should be almost no corner threes. Preferred starting spots: top of the key and the right wing. He drives right or downhill, takes one dribble from the 3-pt line, and uses the Eurostep about 35% of drives, a straight power two-step dunk about 40%, the spin gather about 15%, and a pull-up/kick about 10%. In transition (after a defensive rebound) he grabs and goes himself: coast-to-coast with 3-4 dribbles to a long-gather dunk. Post-ups: if matched against a smaller defender, a short face-up or back-down from the right block, then a spin or drop-step. Passing: a good drive-and-kick passer who looks for the open corner shooter when two defenders collapse. He makes cross-court skip passes and is willing to give it up when doubled. He is not a lob thrower. Screens: rolls hard to the rim as the screener in a 3v3 pick-and-roll; also a lob target. Defence: a roaming 'free safety'. He helps from the weak side, contests at the rim, can switch onto guards for short stretches, and goes for chase-down blocks in transition. He plays passing lanes moderately (steals from deflections with his long arms rather than gambling). As a rebounder he is aggressive on both glasses. Weaknesses for the AI: tends to force drives into crowded paints (offensive foul or charge chance about 4%), shoots a low free-throw percentage (about 66%), and the long FT routine adds time pressure.

profiles.build: Very tall, long and broad, but soft rather than chiselled: the build of a giant, not a bodybuilder. KEY PROPORTION: his head is small relative to his body, about 8.4-8.6 head-heights tall (head about 27 cm, crown to chin), against about 7.5 for the default MakeHuman male. Scaling the base mesh uniformly to 2.29 m gives a head about 30 cm tall, which reads like a big man in a suit. After height scaling, scale the head bone (or the head vertex group) by about 0.90-0.92 and lengthen the neck. This is the most important body fix for all very tall players, Yao most of all. Neck: long, moderately thick, clearly visible above the jersey collar. Shoulders: wide (biacromial about 50-52 cm) but sloping and rounded, with no bulging deltoids or traps. Chest: broad and fairly flat front to back, light pec definition. Torso: long, with a thick, straight waist and little V-taper (at 141 kg the midsection is solid, with no six-pack). Hips and thighs: wide and heavy, and the thighs are the most massive part of the legs. Calves are comparatively slim and long and the knees are large. Arms: long but slightly shorter than his height (wingspan 2.26 m against height 2.29 m, ape index about 0.99, where most NBA athletes are 1.03-1.08). Upper arms are smooth and only moderately muscled, forearms average. Hands: big, long fingers. Feet: US 18 (about 33 cm), which is proportionally normal for 2.29 m, so do NOT enlarge the feet beyond height scaling. Posture: upright and a little stiff, with a slight forward head carriage and rounded upper back when standing. He moves heavily with relatively short strides for his size. Compared with a generic 1.98 m athlete: 31 cm taller, much longer legs and neck, smaller head ratio, wider but softer shoulders, thicker waist and thighs, less muscle definition everywhere, and shorter relative arms.
profiles.face: Head shape: a long rectangular-oval face, clearly longer than it is wide (face height to bizygomatic width about 1.45). The temples are flat, there is no fat on the face at his peak, and the back of the skull is fairly flat. Forehead: high and broad, nearly vertical, about 1/3 of face height, with a straight horizontal hairline. Brow: low, straight, thick black eyebrows with a slight upward tilt at the outer ends, sitting close above the eyes. The brow ridge is only mild. Eyes: dark brown, almost black, with East Asian monolid / low-crease upper lids and a mild epicanthic fold. The eyes are fairly small and narrow relative to the long face, with a slightly almond shape, a nearly horizontal axis or a very slight upward tilt at the outer corners, and normal-to-slightly-wide spacing. The upper lid is heavy, so the eyes look calm and half-lidded in play, and they close almost to slits when he grins. Nose: long and straight, with a moderate bridge that is higher than the typical asian macro default. The lower third is broad: a rounded, fleshy tip and wide, slightly flared nostrils (alar width about the inner-canthal distance plus 25%). The septum is not upturned. Midface: flat to moderately projecting, with high but broad, flat cheekbones and lean cheeks. Mouth: wide, with medium-full lips (the lower lip fuller than the upper), a long philtrum, and corners neutral to slightly downturned at rest. The mouth often hangs slightly open when he runs. Grin: very wide and toothy, showing the upper teeth to the premolars, with cheeks bunching up and eyes squinting. Jaw and chin: a long lower face with a strong, wide mandible that has visible angles (squarish). The chin is long vertically, slightly forward, and broad and rounded rather than pointed. Ears: LARGE and noticeably protruding from the head (very visible under the short haircut), with long lobes. This is a key close-up cue. On court his face is usually calm, earnest and expressionless. He shows a brief determined grimace when posting up, and an open-mouth roar with bared teeth after an and-one or dunk.
profiles.hair: A short, straight, jet-black crew cut. Top: 12-18 mm, straight hair standing up slightly and brushed forward and up at the front, with a slightly flat-topped crown. Sides and back: tapered to 5-8 mm above the ears, with the ears fully exposed and a short natural tapered nape. Hairline: low-to-medium, straight across the forehead, with very slight recession at the temple corners (no widow's peak). Colour: natural black #121010, with a cool, faintly blue-grey specular sheen under arena lights. Hair density is high, so render it as a dark shell or card layer with a short fuzzy edge alpha (no long strands), and let a little scalp tint show through only on the sides. Rookie-era variant (2002-04, not the default): top about 25-30 mm, spiky and messy.
profiles.facialHair: Clean-shaven. At most a barely visible shadow of 0.5 mm stubble on the upper lip and chin (5-10% darkening, colour #2a2420). No moustache, goatee or sideburns below the mid-ear.

signatureMoves: CONVENTIONS for all moves: 30 fps, right-handed shooter, rig.game_engine bone names (pelvis, spine_01/02/03, neck_01, head, clavicle_l/r, upperarm_l/r, lowerarm_l/r, hand_l/r, finger chains, thigh_l/r, calf_l/r, foot_l/r, ball_l/r). Angles are joint rotations from the bind T/A-pose: flex = forward bend, abduct = arm away from body sideways. 'Yaw CCW' is seen from above. Yao's jump heights are SMALL (0.15-0.35 m). His power comes from his height and reach, so do not reuse guard jump curves.

1) RIGHT-HAND JUMP HOOK TO THE MIDDLE FROM THE LEFT BLOCK (primary move). F0: back to the basket on the left block, feet 0.75 m apart, thigh flex 35 deg, calf flex 45 deg, pelvis lowered 0.12 m, spine_01-03 forward flex 5/5/5 deg. Ball 'chinned' at chin height in both hands, upperarm abduct 60 deg, elbows out, lowerarm flex 110 deg. Head yawed 30 deg left to read the defender. F0-6: one hard right-hand dribble: ball drops from chest to the floor 0.3 m outside the right foot and back. spine_02 leans back 8 deg into the defender (shoulder bump), pelvis shifts 0.05 m back. F6-12: left foot steps 0.55 m toward the lane middle and 0.15 m toward the rim. Pelvis yaws CCW 70 deg so the LEFT shoulder points at the rim. Ball gathered with both hands at the right hip, then rising. F12-18: right foot closes to 0.4 m from the left (two-foot jump-hook gather). thigh flex 40 deg. Ball moves to the right ear, right hand under-behind the ball, left hand on its side. F18-28: takeoff at F18, apex at F26 (rise 0.22 m). Left arm becomes a bent shield: upperarm_l abduct 75 deg, lowerarm_l flex 95 deg, forearm horizontal at chest height between ball and defender. Right arm sweeps up in the coronal plane: upperarm_r abduct 95 to 170 deg, lowerarm_r flex 90 to 10 deg. The ball arcs from the right ear outward and over the head. Release at F26 at about 3.45 m off the fingertips, hand_r wrist flex 0 to 60 deg over F24-28. Ball launch angle 55 deg with a soft backspin of about 2 rev/s. head yawed fully toward the rim, neck_01 tilted 10 deg left. F28-38: follow-through. The right arm stays vertical, wrist dropped ('hand in the cookie jar'), and the left arm lowers to 45 deg abduction. Land at F34 on both feet at the same spot (no fade), knees absorbing 30 deg. F38-45: torso turns 20 deg toward the rim to watch the ball.

2) TURNAROUND FADEAWAY JUMPER FROM THE RIGHT BLOCK (over the right shoulder). F0: post-up stance as in move 1, on the right block. F0-8: head fake: head and spine_03 yaw 25 deg left (fake middle), ball dips 0.1 m. F8-16: LEFT foot is the pivot. Pelvis, then spine_01-03, yaw CW 160 deg (over the right shoulder) while the right foot swings back and around 0.5 m to finish square to the rim. The ball travels up the midline from chin to forehead during the turn. Knees load to thigh flex 45 deg. F16-30: takeoff at F16, apex at F24, rise 0.28 m, with backward drift (fade) of 0.35 m away from the rim. Spine leans back 12 deg (spine_02 extend 8, spine_03 extend 4), and the legs trail slightly forward (thigh flex 15 deg). Set point at F20: ball 0.15 m above and 0.1 m in front of the forehead, upperarm_r flex 150 deg, elbow under the ball (lowerarm_r flex 95 deg), right elbow 10 deg out from vertical, left hand on the side of the ball with fingers up. Release at F24 at about 3.55 m: lowerarm_r extends to 5 deg, wrist flex 70 deg over 4 frames, guide hand comes off the ball and stays still with the thumb not flicking. Launch angle 50 deg. F24-36: follow-through held: right hand high with fingers pointing at the rim, guide hand opens sideways. Land at F32 on both feet 0.35 m behind the takeoff point, knees absorbing 35 deg and the torso straightening upright.

3) HIGH-POST FACE-UP JUMPER / PICK-AND-POP (15-18 ft). F0: catch at the elbow facing the rim, triple-threat with the ball at the right hip, thigh flex 30 deg. F0-10 (optional): right-foot jab step 0.3 m toward the rim with a head and shoulder dip of 10 deg, recovering at F10. F10-16: gather: ball rises in front of the chest to the set point above the forehead. Shoulders square, feet shoulder width with the right foot 0.1 m ahead. F16-24: small rise of only 0.15 m (practically a set shot with tiptoe lift), straight up with no fade. Same arm mechanics as move 2: elbow under the ball, release at the apex (F22) at about 3.45 m. High arc: launch 52 deg. F24-36: hold the follow-through, then drop the arms and back-pedal.

4) DROP-STEP TWO-HAND POWER DUNK (left block, baseline drop). F0: post-up on the left block with the defender on the high side. F0-8: RIGHT foot reverse-pivots (drop step): it swings 0.6 m back toward the baseline and rim while pelvis yaws CW 120 deg. Spine_02 seals the defender with a backward lean of 6 deg. Optional one right-hand dribble at F4 with the ball bouncing between the feet. F8-14: two-foot power gather: both feet planted 0.5 m apart facing the rim, deep load (thigh flex 60 deg, calf flex 70 deg), ball pulled to the chest in both hands, elbows out. F14-22: takeoff at F14, apex at F21, rise 0.33 m. Both arms raise the ball overhead: upperarms flex 170 deg, lowerarms flex 20 to 0 deg. F21-23: SLAM. Both hands drive the ball down through the rim (hands_l/r wrist flex 60 deg) and the ball exits downward. F23-28: optional one-hand rim grab with the right hand only, held 3 frames, body swinging 5 deg. F28-36: land on both feet with a heavy knee absorb (thigh flex 50 deg). F36-50: celebration (see mannerisms): torso flexed forward, both fists clenched and pumped down to hip height, mouth open roaring.

5) RIM PROTECTION BLOCK / VERTICALITY CONTEST. Stance: drop coverage within 2.5 m of the rim, feet 0.7 m apart, knees flexed 25 deg, both arms half-raised (upperarm abduct 45 deg, lowerarm flex 60 deg, hands at shoulder height). F0-6: shuffle-step 0.4 m toward the shooter's line (slow lateral speed). F6-10: load (thigh flex 35 deg). F10-18: takeoff at F10, apex at F17, rise 0.30 m. VERTICALITY version: both arms straight up (upperarm flex 175 deg, lowerarm flex 0) with palms forward and the body straight, fingertip height about 3.25 m. BLOCK version: the blocking arm (default left hand vs a right-handed shooter, otherwise the nearer arm) reaches 15 deg forward of vertical. Between F15 and F17, hand flex 50 deg swats the ball down and sideways (ball velocity reverses, out at 6-8 m/s), or a soft tip-to-self flicks the ball upward and back with the wrist 30 deg. The other arm stays vertical. F18-30: land on both feet, arms come down to 90 deg abduction, head tracks the ball, then he turns and jogs.

6) UP-FAKE AND UP-AND-UNDER (counter to the jump hook). F0-6: from the gather of move 1, sharp pump fake: ball goes from the right ear up to the forehead and back in 6 frames, heels lift 0.04 m, head and eyes go up to the rim. F6-12: the defender leaves the floor. The RIGHT foot steps through 0.6 m past the defender's hip toward the rim, the left foot is the pivot, and spine_02 flexes forward 20 deg to duck under. F12-22: one-foot (off the left) or two-foot short lift of 0.15 m, and a right-hand finger-roll lay-in from 2.95 m: upperarm_r flex 160 deg, lowerarm extends, ball off the fingertips with underspin.

7) HIGH-POST / DOUBLE-TEAM OVERHEAD PASS. F0: catch at the elbow or in the post when the second defender arrives. F0-6: ball goes overhead, upperarms flex 165 deg with both hands at the back of the ball, elbows bent 70 deg so the ball is behind the head. Head yaws toward the target. F6-10: arms snap forward (upperarm 165 to 120 deg, lowerarm 70 to 0 deg), thumbs rotate down and the ball releases at about 3.1 m on a flat 4-6 deg line at 10-12 m/s to a cutter or the weak-side shooter. Left foot steps 0.2 m toward the target. F10-18: arms follow through pointing at the target, then relax.

8) DEFENSIVE / OFFENSIVE REBOUND 'CHIN IT'. Box out: hips back, butt into the opponent, thigh flex 40 deg, arms out at 90 deg abduction with the forearms up. On the ball: two-foot jump of only 0.2 m, both arms fully extended overhead (grab height about 3.30 m). Secure with both hands, then F+6: pull the ball to the chin with elbows flared out to 80 deg abduction and the torso slightly rotating left-right 10 deg to clear space.
profiles.shootingForm: Textbook, compact, high and soft. He has the touch of a much smaller player (about 83% career FT, about 52% FG, a good mid-range shooter for a 2.29 m center). Stance: feet shoulder width, right foot 5-10 cm ahead, toes angled about 10 deg left of the rim line. Set point: one-motion (not a two-stage set), ball 10-15 cm above and slightly in front of the forehead, so he shoots over his own head, not from behind it. Shooting elbow directly under the ball, about 10 deg outward. Upper arm flexed to about 150 deg. Forearm vertical with the wrist cocked back 70-80 deg and the ball on the finger pads. Guide (left) hand: on the side of the ball with fingers up. It comes off at release with no thumb flick and stays up as a mirror. Release height: about 3.40-3.55 m on jumpers (higher than anyone in the game), about 3.30 m on free throws. Release at or just before the apex of the jump. Jump: small (0.12-0.20 m) on set jumpers, up to 0.28 m on turnarounds. Fade: none on face-ups, 0.3-0.4 m backward drift on turnaround fadeaways. Arc: medium-high, 50-53 deg launch on jumpers and about 55 deg on hooks (hooks are soft lobs). Backspin about 2 rev/s. Follow-through: held until the ball reaches the rim, arm straight, wrist fully flexed with the fingers pointing at the rim (index and middle finger last to touch). Free throw: almost no jump, just a rise onto the toes (heels up 4 cm). Quirks: very little dip before the shot (the ball goes straight from the catch to the set point) and very slow, deliberate rhythm. He almost never shoots threes (keep the 3PT attempt rate under 1%).
mannerisms: And-one / big dunk roar: legs planted wide, torso flexed forward 20 deg, both fists clenched and pumped down to hip height (or one fist pumped once) with elbows bent. Mouth wide open, bared teeth, eyes squinted, a short yell of 1-1.5 s, then he jogs back nodding.
Big toothy grin: a wide smile that shows the upper teeth, cheeks bunched, eyes closing to slits. Used on the bench, after a teammate's play, in menu idle and on the player card.

Free-throw routine: toes just behind the line, right foot slightly forward. Receives the ball, then two or three slow right-hand bounce dribbles with knees slightly bent, rotates the ball once in his hands to find the seams, a short pause looking at the rim, one smooth lift to the set point, a rise onto the toes and release, holding the follow-through until the ball drops.

High fives and chest bumps adapted to his height: he bends forward at the waist (spine flex 25 deg) or lowers his hand to teammates' head height, and gives pats on the back or head after a timeout or a basket.

Idle and dead-ball stance: upright, hands on hips or hands resting on his knees with straight arms (spine flex 40 deg) during opponent free throws. He also tugs at the waistband of his shorts with both hands.

Calm demeanour: neutral, earnest, almost expressionless face during play, with occasional lip-pursing or a quick exhale through puffed cheeks after a long possession. After a block he does not taunt. He turns and runs the floor, sometimes pointing to a teammate to leak out.

Running gait: upright torso with very little forward lean, relatively short heavy strides, arms swinging low with forearms near horizontal, a slight side-to-side sway of the shoulders and head. He backpedals slowly on defence and his transition speed is noticeably the slowest on the floor.

Defensive posture: long arms held up and wide (verticality) when a guard drives. When sealing he raises the left arm for the entry pass with the palm open as a target, and calls for the ball with an open right hand at head height in the post.
Post-up seal: wide base, left forearm on the defender's back, right hand raised high (about 2.9 m) as the target, head turned over the right shoulder toward the passer.
profiles.tendencies: Role: post scorer and rim protector. He is the slowest player on the floor, so the AI should never ask him to beat anyone off the dribble. OFFENSE: Spots are the left and right low blocks (60% of touches) and the elbows / high post (35%). He almost never goes beyond 5.5 m (no threes; 3PA rate under 1%). He rarely sets up outside the paint except to screen. Shot selection when he has the ball in the post: right-hand jump hook to the middle 30%, turnaround fadeaway 15%, drop-step dunk or power layup when sealed deep under 1.5 m 15%, up-fake into up-and-under 5%, pass out of the post 30% (always pass if doubled within 0.8 s: overhead pass to the open shooter or a cutter), and 5% reset by kicking back out. At the high post: catch-and-shoot or one-jab face-up jumper 55%, high-low or cutter pass 35%, hand-off / re-screen 10%. Pick-and-roll: he sets high screens and mostly POPS to the elbow (65%) rather than rolling (35%). Dribbles: max 2 per possession, never a crossover. Drive tendency very low (5%). Transition: trails the play and posts at the block. Offensive rebounding: high crash rate (60%) and tip-ins. He is fouled often and shoots free throws well, so in close games the AI should feed him the post to draw fouls. DEFENSE: Drop coverage. Anchors within 2.5 m of the rim on every possession, does not switch onto guards on the perimeter (late, slow closeouts and weak lateral speed), and helps from the weak side. Contest style: verticality first (straight arms up, low foul rate). Goes for the block only when the ball is below his reach and the shooter is within 2 m: block attempt probability high in the paint, near zero outside 4 m. Steal attempts are rare (no gambling). Always boxes out. Prioritises the defensive rebound over leaking out. Guards opposing bigs in the post with a wide base. Against Giannis or LeBron drives he stays home under the rim and contests rather than stepping up early. In 3v3 he should be the clear rim deterrent: opponents' shot success in his zone gets a strong reach/height penalty, but quick guards (Kyrie) beat him in space.

profiles.build: Compact, low-slung lead guard: 1.88 m and 88 kg, with about 10% body fat at the combine. Compared with a generic 1.98 m athlete he is 10 cm shorter and much more compact. He is not bulky on top and his shoulders are only moderately wide (about 44-45 cm biacromial). His trapezius and deltoids are defined but not big, and the V-taper is mild to moderate. His chest is flat to moderately muscled. His waist is narrow and his stomach flat and tight. The weight sits low, in thick, powerful thighs, round glutes and strong calves, which gives him the low centre of gravity behind his change of direction. His arms are average length for his height (wingspan 1.93 m, ape index about +2 in over barefoot height) and lean, with defined forearms. His hands are SMALL for an NBA player: 8.25 in long and 9.25 in wide, so keep hand scale slightly under default. His neck is medium length and moderately thick. Torso and legs are close to average proportion, with a slightly long torso. His natural stance is athletic: knees always a little bent, hips low, chest over the ball.
profiles.face: Overall a slim, slightly long oval face, narrower than LeBron's or Giannis's, with a calm, composed look. HEAD: oval to slightly rectangular, moderately long, a little narrow at the temples. FOREHEAD: fairly high and smooth, with a straight, sharply lined-up hairline. BROWS: dark, thick, fairly straight and low, sitting close above the eyes, giving a level, focused look. EYES: dark brown and almond-shaped, with moderately heavy upper lids and a slightly sleepy, relaxed look. Medium spacing, outer corners level or very slightly upturned, faint under-eye fullness. NOSE: medium length with a straight, moderately wide bridge, a rounded, fairly broad tip and medium-wide, gently flared nostrils. Not as broad as Jordan's or LeBron's. LIPS: full, especially the lower lip, with a defined cupid's bow. Mouth is medium-wide, framed by the moustache. JAW and CHIN: narrow-to-medium jaw, with a chin that projects slightly and is a little long. Most of the jaw outline is defined by the beard. CHEEKBONES: prominent and fairly high, with lean, slightly hollow cheeks beneath them, a key part of his look. EARS: medium-small, lying close to the head. ON-COURT EXPRESSION: neutral and unreadable, often with the mouthguard half out of his mouth or being chewed. He gives a small closed-mouth smirk after tough makes.
profiles.hair: Short, dense, tightly coiled black hair (#141010). Length is about 8-12 mm on top and about 4-6 mm on the sides, blending into a low-to-medium taper or fade with no skin showing in the Cleveland era. The edge-up is crisp: hairline straight across the forehead, sharp squared temple corners and a clean line around the ears. The shape is slightly rounded on top and close to the skull, with no part and no designs. Render it as a short dark shell over the scalp with a fine noise or coil normal map and a hard alpha edge at the hairline. In the Mavericks alternate, the top is a little longer (15-20 mm).
profiles.facialHair: Full, well-groomed beard, black (#121010), dense and even. The cheek line is high and sharply shaped, running straight from the sideburn down to the corner of the moustache (about 1.5 cm below the cheekbone). It connects to the sideburns and to the shaped hairline. Length is about 8-12 mm on the jaw and chin and a little fuller at the chin (about 12-15 mm), giving a slightly squared, rounded chin outline. The moustache is full but trimmed above the upper lip and connects into the beard at the mouth corners. The lower-lip patch is filled in. The neckline is clean, about 2 cm above the Adam's apple. In the Mavericks alternate the beard is longer and denser (15-25 mm at the chin). At 120 px tall the beard must read as a clear dark mass along the jaw and chin. This is the number-one cue that sets him apart from clean-shaven Jordan and Kobe.

signatureMoves: HESI-CROSSOVER (right to left), 30 fps, 20 frames. F0: attacking dribble with the right hand, pelvis about 0.95 m high, torso leaning 15 degrees forward, ball at hip height outside the right foot. F0-4, the hesitation: the right foot plants slightly ahead and the pelvis RISES about 6 cm while spine02-03 straighten to about 5 degrees of lean. The head lifts and looks at the rim as if to shoot, the left arm floats out at about 30 degrees of abduction, and the ball is carried high (about 0.85 m) on a soft right-hand dribble. F5-7, the drop: the pelvis drops about 10 cm, knees bend about 60 degrees and the torso snaps back to 25 degrees of lean. The right hand pushes the ball low and hard across the body: one bounce, ball below knee height (0.25-0.35 m), bouncing midway between the feet. F8-9: the ball is caught by the left hand outside the left knee, and the right shoulder (clavicle) dips and rotates toward the defender to shield. F10-14, the explosion: the left foot pushes off, the right thigh drives across and forward, and the pelvis yaws 30 degrees to the left. Head stays level and eyes stay on the rim. F15-20: long first step and drive at a 20-degree lean, with a left-hand dribble ahead of the left foot.

DOUBLE BETWEEN-THE-LEGS INTO STEP-BACK THREE (the 2016 Game 7 shot), 36 frames, right wing. F0-6: wide stance, feet 0.7 m apart and left foot forward. The right hand bounces the ball between the legs, front to back, to the left hand, angled under the pelvis at a 15 cm bounce height. Torso leans 20 degrees and the head is still. F7-12: the left hand sends it back between the legs to the right hand while the feet scissor (right foot forward). Rhythm is quick and loose, with the pelvis bobbing ±3 cm. F13-16, the jab: the right foot jabs 25 cm toward the defender and the shoulders dip forward as the ball goes low and right. F17-21, the step-back: the right foot pushes off and the body hops BACK 0.7-0.9 m. The left foot lands first, then the right lands beside it about 0.4 m apart, and the ball is gathered with both hands at the right hip during the hop. F22-26: the knees load (about 70 degrees) and the ball rises along the chest to the set point above the right eye. F27-32: jump about 0.35 m with a slight 5-10 degree fade back, release at the top, wrist snap. F33-36: the follow-through is held and the landing comes about 15 cm behind the takeoff point.

SPIN MOVE (reverse pivot) INTO LEFT-HAND FINISH, 24 frames. F0-3: driving right with a right-hand dribble, then a hard plant of the LEFT foot ahead and across, knee about 70 degrees, braking. F4-6: the ball is pulled by the right hand to the right hip (palm on top, close to the body), the head turns over the left shoulder toward the rim before the body follows, and the torso begins to yaw. F7-12, the spin: the pelvis rotates about 270 degrees counter-clockwise (viewed from above) around the planted left foot. The right leg swings round wide and low, clavicles stay level, and the ball stays tight to the right hip, then switches to the left hand at about 200 degrees of rotation. Arms stay close to the body, with elbows within 15 cm of the torso. F13-15: the right foot lands toward the rim, the ball is gathered in both hands, the step is long, and the pelvis drops for a one-foot (right-foot) takeoff. F16-24: jump about 0.5 m and finish with the left hand up and off the glass: arm extended, wrist under the ball, fingers rolling it up. The right arm shields at shoulder height.

REVERSE LAYUP WITH ENGLISH OFF THE GLASS (baseline drive from the right side), 30 frames. F0-6: drive along the right baseline under the rim, last dribble with the right hand, ball gathered at about F6 with the left foot down and the body leaning 20 degrees toward the baseline. F7-10: plant the right foot under the front of the rim (or two-foot jump), knees about 60 degrees, eyes looking up and back over the LEFT shoulder at the glass. The torso has already passed under the rim, so the back is to the opposite baseline. F11-18: jump about 0.55 m. The spine leans back about 10 degrees and twists 40 degrees toward the rim while the head looks up and back at the backboard. The RIGHT arm extends straight overhead and slightly behind the head, hand under the ball with the palm facing the glass. On release the wrist and fingers flick left-to-right to give heavy SIDESPIN. Ball path: up and back onto the glass about 0.3 m left of the rim's centre line and 0.4 m above the rim, then it kisses off with spin and drops into the rim's far side. F18-22: the left arm extends out to shield against the shot-blocker. F23-30: land on two feet on the opposite side of the rim, facing the far corner.

HIGH FLOATER / TEARDROP (and the Kyrie 'scoop'), 22 frames, about 3-4 m from the rim, in the lane. F0-4: drive with the right hand into the lane and pick up the ball off the LEFT foot early, a 'one-two' gather at about 4.5 m. F5-8: takeoff off ONE foot (the left) or a quick two-foot hop, with no full gathering dip: knees only about 35 degrees, so it is quick. The body rises nearly vertical with a slight forward drift (0.2-0.3 m). F9-13: the right arm extends up and forward at about 60 degrees from horizontal, ball in the fingertips. At about F12 there is a soft high release with a fingertip flip and backspin, much earlier than a layup, before the big man can reach. Arc is very high, peaking about 1.8 m above the rim, about 70 degrees on the way up. F14-18: the wrist relaxes and the arm stays up, while the free (left) arm angles out for balance. F19-22: soft landing, often on one foot, then hands down. Variant: the 'underhand scoop' is the same approach with a lower takeoff, the ball pulled down to the hip and released underhand from below waist height with the arm sweeping forward and up and a spinning flick off the glass from wide angles.

BEHIND-THE-BACK INTO PULL-UP MIDRANGE: going right, a hard stop with both feet planted wide (0.6 m). The right hand wraps the ball behind the back across the lower lumbar region (at pelvis height, bounce behind the heels) to the left hand while the body keeps moving right. The defender overruns, the ball is gathered off the left-hand bounce in 2 frames, and the pull-up comes off a two-foot hop with no extra dribble, using the same shooting form.
profiles.shootingForm: Right-handed. The shot is compact and quick, close to a one-motion shot, and he gets it off fast from any dribble. The dip is short: catch, ball drops to chest or belly height (about 1.1 m) for 1-2 frames, then rises up the midline. The set point is above and slightly in front of the right eye or forehead. The release is quite high for a guard, at about 2.55 m standing (higher at the top of the jump), and comes just before or at the apex. The right elbow is tucked, pointing at the rim, with the forearm vertical at the set point. The left guide hand sits on the left side of the ball with the thumb up and comes off cleanly at release without pushing the ball; it stays up beside the shot about 10 cm away. Follow-through: full elbow extension, wrist snapped, fingers pointing at the rim, held for about 0.4 s. Arc is medium-high (45-50 degrees launch). The jump is moderate on catch-and-shoot (about 0.3 m) and higher on pull-ups. He lands with toes slightly forward, legs apart. On step-backs and contested pull-ups he fades back 5-15 degrees and can drift sideways, and he keeps the same set point when off balance. The shot release time is about 0.45-0.5 s from gather. Quirks: the ball spins very cleanly with tight backspin; he often keeps the shooting hand up after a make and walks back with it held; and he can hit tough contested 'off-balance' twos and threes at almost the same form. Free throw: he takes the ball, spins it in his hands to find the seams, takes 2-3 dribbles, a short exhale, then the same compact shot with a smaller jump (essentially a set shot, heels slightly lifting).
mannerisms: Mouthguard: chews it and lets it hang half out of his mouth during dead balls and while bringing the ball up
After a big make: a small closed-mouth smirk, a raised eyebrow or a blank stare at the defender; no wild screaming
Points one finger skyward or taps his chest over the heart after key shots or at the free throw line (spiritual gesture)
Occasionally holds a finger to his lips ('shh') toward a hostile crowd after a dagger
After a dagger three: holds the follow-through, then backpedals with the arm still up, or turns and walks away slowly
Idle: low dribbling stance, constantly working the ball through crossovers and between the legs while waiting at the top (never a dead, static dribble); drapes the ball in the fingertips
Pre-game and dead balls: spins the ball on his index finger or wraps it around his waist
Hands on hips or on the knees and shorts during free throws by others; often walks with a slight bounce
Free throw: spins the ball in his hands, 2-3 dribbles, breath out, compact shot; holds the follow-through
Bows or nods slightly to the crowd after taking over a game (Uncle Drew-style 'professor' energy); shoulders relaxed
profiles.tendencies: The primary ball-handler with the highest isolation tendency (about 35% of possessions), and he starts most possessions at the top of the key or the right wing. Shot diet: about 40% drives finishing at the rim (layups only; he almost never dunks in traffic, so dunk only on open breaks), about 25% pull-up midrange (elbows and right baseline, often after a step-back or behind-the-back stop), about 25% threes (step-back threes from the right wing and top, catch-and-shoot in the corners), and about 10% floaters from 3-4 m in the lane against bigs. Each isolation chains 2-4 dribble moves (hesitation, between-the-legs, crossover, behind-the-back) before the decision. He prefers driving right but finishes equally with either hand. Against a big who can protect the rim (Yao, Giannis), use a reverse layup on the far side of the rim or a floater rather than finishing straight-on. He attacks switches onto bigs every time. Passing: a capable lead guard, but he looks for his own shot first. Kick-outs come only when doubled, with an occasional lob pass to a rolling big. Pick-and-roll: uses the screen, rejects it about 30% of the time and splits the hedge. Late clock or a tied game in the last 24 s: always isolation, step-back three or pull-up (clutch boost). Defence: decent hands and quick reaction; gambles for steals off the dribble and in passing lanes (steal tendency high). Undersized against posts, so the AI should help and switch him off bigs; minimal shot-blocking, so he does not contest at the rim. Rebounding: leaks out, does not crash the glass.

Wingspan: macro-only MakeHuman tall males already have a wingspan/height ratio of about 1.06. The profile arm-length targets therefore overshot the listed wingspans: Giannis 2.48 m vs 2.21, LeBron 2.37 vs 2.14, Kobe and Jordan +6 cm. Arm length (upper and lower together) is now a solved knob. All six wingspans match their listed values within 0.2 cm.

Head size and shape: the profiles' boosts to forehead-scale-vert, forehead-nubian, head-oval and head-scale-vert produced domed, oversized heads. Jordan was 7.4 heads tall, Yao's head was 28.9 cm, and Giannis's crown/face ratio was 1.35. Forehead height is now solved for a crown-to-eye vs eye-to-chin ratio of 0.98-1.05, and head-scale-vert for head height. Head heights are now: Kobe 24.0 cm, Jordan 24.5, LeBron 24.5, Giannis 23.2 (9.0 heads tall, the smallest ratio as the profile wants), Yao 26.4 (8.6 heads), Kyrie 23.2.

Yao: dropped the profile's post-scale fix (head ×0.91, neck ×1.06). With height "auto", MakeHuman's height targets already keep the head small: macro-only Yao has a 24 cm head, 9.4 heads tall. His chest was the narrowest of the six (0.328 m), contradicting 'broad'. Added torso-scale-horiz 0.4 and measure-bust-circ 0.2, giving 0.345 m, with shoulder joints at 0.49 m.

LeBron: the stacked bulk targets gave an estimated mass of 150 kg. Neck, chest, bust, arm-circumference, thigh and calf targets are roughly halved, while arm/delt/pec/lat muscle is kept high. Shoulder joints went from 0.49 to 0.505 so he is clearly the broadest. Estimated mass is 118.6 kg, which makes him the densest body (BMI 28.8 vs Yao 26.9). Macro weight is 0.25, i.e. low fat.

Giannis: dropped forehead-nubian and head-oval, and raised chin-height to 0.85 for a long lower face. His macro skull is inherently domed, so his craniumFace target is 1.05 and the two head knobs sit at the ±1 limits. Shoulder joints are 0.485 m (high and broad, below LeBron). He has the longest legs of the six (leg ratio 0.522 vs 0.49-0.51), big hands (25.2 cm) and feet (32.5 cm), and a narrow waist.

Mass: macro muscle actually lowers volume at fixed height, so macro weight is the mass knob. Mesh volume × 1.12 reproduces the listed weights of the macro-only bodies. Final estimates: kobe 96.0, jordan 97.9, lebron 118.6, giannis 109.5, yao 138.5, kyrie 88.4 kg.

Stats consistency: listed wingspans and weights were adopted as targets and matched. Jordan's standing-reach estimate went from 2.67 to 2.65 to match Kobe, who has the same height and wingspan. After calibration, every model overhead reach (arms straight up, no shoulder shrug) sits 22-26 cm below the listed reach, so the six reach figures are mutually consistent. By the listed numbers, Kobe and Jordan have the highest ape index (1.077) and Giannis 1.058. Giannis reads as longest-limbed through his legs, forearms, hands and small head, not his ape index.
